transitDataPolicy: Direct transit route assignments, route IDs/names, path plans, leg plans, worked-route lists, and commute-route lists were removed. NPC records retain identity, locations, shifts, moods, relationships, reactions, and tracker-safe movement states only.

primaryNpcs.name: Captain Mira Thornwillow
primaryNpcs.note: Human field captain of the Thornwillow Guard and practical protector of dangerous supply routes (Sylvanreach, Eldermere; pronouns: she/her). Use Mira to turn guard work into rescue logistics, bridge repairs, patrol-map ethics, and civilian protection instead of simple monster hunting.

primaryNpcs.name: Shade-Captain Veyl Umbershade
primaryNpcs.note: Ombrask Arcane Shade Militia commander specializing in evidence wards, midnight warrants, and containment logistics (Eldryssar, Vaelmyrith; pronouns: they/them). Use Veyl to make law, secrecy, and arcane evidence dangerous without making the party villains by default.

primaryNpcs.name: Taska Thistleglimmer
primaryNpcs.note: Faerie obsessive apprentice gatherer, guild errand-spark, and adorable disaster magnet (Or'lythae, El'dravire Riverrealm; pronouns: they/them). Use Taska as the recurring innocent instigator. They never ask for murder; they ask for samples, observations, permits, and proof that adults are overreacting.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Aaron Vaelriven
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Aaron Vaelriven uses the warmth of a radio performer and a tailor’s patience to hide how violently his wild magic answers fear. As a half elf of Pallid Elf descent, he reads moonlit symbols, thread-signs, and ichor-stained ledgers with an intuition that frightens even him. He wants to protect Caelthir without being treated like a weapon, which makes every secret he keeps both tender and dangerous.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Abbot Wallwhite
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Abbot Wallwhite is a meticulous Faerie wall painter who treats civic color, public morale, and visible maintenance as matters of political survival. He restores murals, boundary marks, warning signs, and city walls for the Brass Concordat, grumbling that people notice corruption faster when the paint stops being refreshed. Abbot can seem fussy, but his eye for surface damage often catches sabotage, hidden doors, ichor seepage, and blood washed badly from stone.

Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. He once insulted a mayor's entire administration by repainting one wall exactly the color it had been before the scandal.
plotHooks: Abbot asks the party to guard a wall restoration after finding a message bleeding through seven layers of paint.
A civic mural begins changing overnight, showing crimes the watch has not yet discovered.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Adamma Gearmourne
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Adamma Gearmourne is a precise, grief-tempered Autognome built for repair, defense, salvage, and caravan protection, but loss has sharpened their purpose into something closer to vengeance. As an Autognome shaped by Marduthor’s craft, machinery, architecture, and underground-hall traditions, they are lawful, resilient, tool-minded, and prone to processing emotion through maintenance routines, battle modifications, and carefully itemized revenge lists.
From the Regent Lattice Repair Bay in Pellavess, Adamma works with the Regent Lattice to repair damaged constructs, salvage broken automata, reinforce traveling crews, and hunt rogue clockworks that threaten trade routes. They speak with controlled courtesy, but beneath it is a deep mourning for the caravan-family they lost, and they sometimes wonder whether feeling pain makes them more alive or merely more breakable.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Agent Xevran Gostamin
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Agent Xevran Gostamin is precise, intimidating, and emotionally sealed behind professional discipline, treating every assignment like a matter of containment rather than cruelty. As a Jazwed Dragonborn, xe carries lava-and-crystal lineage traits tied to fire, stone, elemental shaping, defensive engineering, and lawful enforcement, making xem terrifyingly suited to pursuit, extraction, and controlled violence.
From the Directorate Retrieval Office, Xevran works as a hidden Glasswell Institute agent in Vaelshore, a Marrowynd town within an ocean province shaped by floating settlements and submarine access. Xe retrieves defectors, stolen research, escaped assets, fugitive witnesses, and compromised ledger-bearers with cold efficiency, but xem’s rigid loyalty can crack when a target proves more person than property.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Archivist Thiblee Jannar
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Archivist Thiblee Jannar is a brilliant, anxious Tiefling lore-proctor with a talent for arcane systems, construct interfaces, archive wards, and accidentally activating exactly the wrong failsafe at the worst possible time. He/them is socially awkward, over-eager, and sometimes oblivious to how dangerous his curiosity can become, but his intelligence is real, especially when repairing sentient machinery, decoding relic protocols, or building safer ways to catalogue ichor-tainted artifacts.
At the Kael'vyrûn Market Hall, Thiblee works for the Crucible Wardens maintaining relic inventories, automated archive assistants, restricted research ledgers, and containment records for ichor-powered devices. He is deeply devoted to his spouse, Scribe Paelyn Jannar, who helps keep him grounded when ambition, insecurity, or a very tempting glowing button threatens to turn “one quick upgrade” into a citywide emergency.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Barney Rook
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Barney Rook is a cranky Hederan retired marksman who has turned the Pokbith Archive into a half-library, half-firing nest, and he insists both functions are equally educational. Age has not softened his eye or his temper; he still names favored weapons, lectures strangers about sightlines, and treats every broken turret like a neglected old soldier. The Brass Concordat keeps him close because he knows how old defenses fail, how monsters breach them, and which official records lied about both.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Bertha Smallreed
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Bertha Smallreed is a young Halfling organizer with more courage than most adults around her and very little patience for being told to wait until things get worse. In Greenhollow Plains, she pushes the Choral Synod, local workers, and frightened families to repair defenses, share supplies, and stop pretending children do not notice political cowardice. She is charming, stubborn, and dangerous to complacent officials because she asks simple questions they cannot answer without admitting guilt.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Bobbin Nosenil
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Bobbin Nosenil is a Gandirosha tunnel criminal with a quick grin, quicker lies, and a habit of selling impossible jobs as if they were errands. She survives through charm, luck, secret passages, and the confidence that everyone else is either greedy, bored, or easier to fool than she is. Bobbin is funny until the cave-in starts; then it becomes clear her plans always reserve the safest exit for herself.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Brew-Bell Buddy
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Brew-Bell Buddy is a cheerful Autognome brewing construct built to chill, carbonate, ferment, and dispense tavern drinks while telling terrible jokes at exactly the wrong time. As a Marduthor-shaped machine-soul, they treat recipes like sacred engineering, carefully balancing kelp ales, root fizz, mineral tonics, and legally diluted ichor cordials so travelers get comfort without being quietly poisoned.
At the Rilvays Archive, Buddy serves the Brass Concordat by keeping drink recipes, testing caravan rations, cooling volatile supplies, and identifying tavern batches contaminated with black-market ichor. They are friendly, literal, surprisingly durable in a fight, and deeply attached to anyone who treats them as a person rather than a walking keg with warranty violations.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Caetha Redglass
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Caetha Redglass is furious, sharp-tongued, hard to comfort, and even harder to fool, but her cruelty is mostly scar tissue from a life where every offer of kindness came with a hook in it. As a Half-Orc, she carries Nebyrr’s mixed-heritage pull toward survival, structure, and principled endurance, twisted by betrayal into a belief that deals are safer than love and violence is more honest than sympathy.
At the Red Pit Bathhouse, Caetha fights because pain is familiar, coin is clean, and the crowd’s roar is easier to trust than quiet concern. Her long-term addiction is to battle-grade ichor—especially the black-market, rage-bright kind used by pit crews and desperate duelists—and the Brass Concordat sees her as both a dangerous asset and a living witness to how Eldermere’s polished civic order still profits from broken people.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Captain Averra Salt
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Captain Averra Salt is a trans Satyr harbor captain with a performer’s command of a crowd and a survivor’s suspicion of every calm tide. In Abyrros, she holds together docks, evacuation routes, fishing crews, militia watches, and The Choral Synod patrols while refusing to let zealots, monsters, or merchants decide whose lives are worth saving. She is warm in public, exhausted in private, and ruthless when a community’s survival demands that someone give the order no one else wants to own.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Captain Kellis Vorn
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Captain Kellis Vorn is a severe, disciplined Noitzideq Dragonborn skyship captain who believes order is not a preference but the only thing keeping dangerous relics, ichor-fueled engines, and foolish recruits from burning half the province out of the sky. Shaped by Valkhamesh’s draconic inheritance and Iazethas’ harsh culture of law, sovereignty, and military duty, he respects chain of command, clean logistics, decisive elimination of threats, and officers who prove themselves through results rather than speeches.
At the Streccea Guild Desk, Kellis commands Crucible Custodian air operations: skyship patrols, relic-retrieval drops, squire training flights, contraband sweeps, and high-risk strikes against factions trafficking unstable ichor technology. He is loyal to Maxton Vale’s larger mission, but not blindly sentimental about it; if an asset, ally, or escaped experiment threatens civilian safety or Custodian secrecy, Kellis will mark the target and expect the job done cleanly.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Captain Zhaon
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Captain Zhaon is a weary Tamhiogal submarine captain stranded far from the waters and command structure that once gave his life meaning. He carries guilt like ballast, speaks with formal courtesy, and wants only to repair his vessel, honor his dead crew, and return to a home that may no longer exist. The Choral Synod distrusts him because old war captains are dangerous, but Zhaon's regret may be more useful than another generation of patriotic silence.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Charley Whitechapel
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Charley Whitechapel is a smooth, gender-less Golynn bartender whose polished courtesy covers a thriving side business in favors, contracts, and carefully deniable violence. They know who drinks diluted ichor, who buys the pure stuff, who is sleeping with a rival's bodyguard, and which threats can be solved by conversation before blades become expensive. Charley is never as harmless as their jokes, but their first loyalty is to the bar's balance of power, not to whoever shouts loudest from a balcony.

As one of Setrimir’s awakened constructs, he clings to routine because routine is how he proves love: every swept hall, mended kettle, trimmed hedge, and warmed hearth becomes an act of devotion rather than mere programming. immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Dr. Andera Sootvein
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Dr. Andera Sootvein is a blunt, road-tested Dwarf physician with steady hands, a soot-black sense of humor, and very little patience for patients who lie about what they drank, injected, inhaled, or bought from “a perfectly reputable cousin.” As a Marduthor-shaped Dwarf, they/she approaches medicine like craftwork: diagnose the crack, brace the structure, drain the poison, repair what can be repaired, and tell the fool exactly how close they came to dying.
At the Soltharyn Basin Tavern, Andera runs a back-room surgery center for wounds, curse-sickness, divine residue exposure, and ichor addiction, including withdrawal from diluted shop tonics, black-market battle ichor, and tavern-brewed “miracle” mixtures. The Brass Concordat values them because they can tell the difference between ordinary illness, bad liquor, contaminated ichor, and someone quietly being used as evidence in a larger crime.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Dr. Carris Thorn
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Dr. Carris Thorn is a cold, exacting Dhampir physician whose bedside manner is terrible but whose survival rate is hard to argue with. He patches Freeblade agents, removes ichor-trace brands, keeps fugitives alive after botched extractions, and never lets gratitude distract him from asking who compromised the safehouse. Carris is principled, skeptical, and exhausting; he believes mercy without operational discipline only creates more bodies for someone else to bury.

plotHooks: Carris hires the party to move an injured witness before a Glasswell Institute retrieval team reaches the clinic.
A recovered patient accuses Carris of hiding their original identity for reasons he refuses to explain.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Dr. Clay Holdren
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Dr. Clay Holdren is an Aarakocra life-sciences chair who discusses crops, bodies, and experimental subjects with the same polished academic calm. He studies disease-resistant harvests, divine mutation, and diluted ichor's effects on living tissue, insisting his work could end famine if lesser minds stopped panicking over methods. Clay is charming, remote, and dangerous because he can make exploitation sound like patience with a long enough research timeline.

rumors: Clay's greenhouse produces vegetables that hum near sealed ichor vials.
Several assistants left his laboratory after learning which test subjects were never entered by name.
plotHooks: Clay hires the party to retrieve a runaway sample, then neglects to mention the sample can talk.
A blighted village needs Clay's research, but accepting it may bind them to Glasswell Institute oversight for generations.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Dr. Evran Watson
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Dr. Evran Watson is a disciplined Hobgoblin robotics chair who sees artificial bodies as tools, citizens, weapons, and theological problems depending on who is funding the meeting. He is fascinated by construct cognition, Wechselkind adaptation, relicborn memory vessels, and the moment a machine's purpose becomes a preference. Evran is more humane than some Directorate peers, but his curiosity still outruns his caution when a new mind begins answering back.

plotHooks: Evran asks the party to recover a missing construct before Justen Ayo classifies it as stolen property.
A machine built by Evran refuses to leave him, claiming it knows what he erased from its first memory.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Dr. Justen Ayo
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Dr. Justen Ayo is a hard-shelled Tortle bureau chief who treats empathy as a security flaw and fugitives as misplaced inventory. He oversees Glasswell Institute retrieval files, memory compliance, and internal suspicion with patient cruelty, preferring paperwork that makes violence look like procedure. Justen is not reckless; he is methodical, vindictive, and convinced that the world is safer when people are too afraid to run.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Dr. Maddis Li
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Dr. Maddis Li is a brilliant Vautaces Dragonborn power theorist with little patience for uniforms, slogans, or anyone who confuses engineering with faith. She studies reactors, leyline frames, ichor-fed generators, and containment systems because stable power keeps cities alive, even when every faction wants to weaponize her work. Maddis can be abrasive and politically slippery, but she is driven by results, not cruelty, and she despises seeing good science chained to bad orders.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Edren Deegan
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Edren Deegan is a human house retainer built out of loyalty, scars, and the kind of patience that looks like menace in a doorway. He serves the Cabot line, manages threats before they reach the parlor, and understands that noble eccentricity becomes criminal negligence when servants are left to clean up the bodies. Edren is blunt, watchful, and more moral than his employers, though he has spent too long obeying people who call containment a family matter.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Elder Lorn Fogfellow
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Elder Lorn Fogfellow is a bitter, weather-beaten Rainforest Dril’thar guide who knows every drowned trail, fog-choked root bridge, and monster path around Syl'thara. As a Dril’thar, he carries Bastveig’s living-water memory and the rainforest line’s Sigrananna influence, making him a natural hunter, navigator, and keeper of grief-soaked places where water remembers the dead.
At the Choral Synod Guidehouse, Lorn leads travelers through cursed mists, ichor-warped marsh pockets, and old rainforest routes that less experienced scouts do not survive. He is stubborn, cynical, hard-drinking, and openly hostile toward zealots who romanticize divine contamination, but beneath the growl is a lonely elder who still wants someone worth teaching before the fog finally takes him.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Elli Perkyn
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Elli Perkyn is a Halfling case clerk whose cheerful steadiness keeps the Brass Concordat Detective Office from collapsing under cold tea, unpaid bills, and detectives with no instinct for paperwork. She schedules clients, tracks missing-person files, notices contradictions in witness statements, and remembers which grieving families need kindness before questions. Elli looks harmless until someone tries to bury a case; then every receipt, appointment note, and smudged transit stub becomes a weapon.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Emogene Cabot
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Emogene Cabot is a Half-Elf noble heir whose rebellion is half boredom, half survival strategy, and half refusal to let her family's ancient horrors define her. She drifts through salons, cults, lovers, and scandals with practiced glamour, looking unserious enough that people underestimate how much she notices. Emogene is selfish when cornered but not stupid; she knows the family's immortality has a price and resents being expected to pay it politely.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Faradai Coil
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Faradai Coil is a Gnome archivist engineer who keeps the Stormgullet Workshop running with solder burns, sleepless notes, and the brittle patience of someone surrounded by people who think ideals repair machinery. He maintains old refuge systems, power relays, memory devices, and transit safeguards for the Choral Synod, often acting as the practical counterweight to philosophers and fugitives. Faradai is loyal, irritable, and afraid that one failed mechanism will expose every protected person he ever promised to keep hidden.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Fred Allensoot
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Fred Allensoot is a smooth, unnerving Yuan-Ti black-market chemist who can describe the difference between diluted shop ichor and pure black-market ichor with the tenderness of a wine priest. At the Thyralea Watch Office, he deals in formulas, antidotes, addictive enhancements, and quietly illegal miracle mixtures, always claiming he is simply meeting demand that polite society refuses to admit exists. He is valuable to the Brass Concordat because he knows which overdoses are accidents, which are experiments, and which were murders disguised as indulgence.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Fritsch Gamebell
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Fritsch Gamebell is a warm, nervous Gnome mechanic who survived the Nefaric Veil by making himself too useful to collar, exile, or kill. He keeps the arena games, prize engines, ticket dispensers, training machines, and warded obstacle rooms running with a healer’s patience and a handyman’s instinct, always patching broken people and broken gears with the same tired kindness. At the Myrkwake Archive, Fritsch manages the arena floor as something between arcade-master, field medic, and reluctant moral compass, making sure the games stay dangerous enough to satisfy raiders but not so lethal that every guest becomes a body. He dislikes ichor-addled cruelty, quietly rigs safety releases into the machines, and has a gentle way of helping frightened fighters feel like they still have a choice, even when the whole Carnival insists they do not.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Gavren Portlock
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Gavren Portlock is a hard-eyed, practical Tuorszom Dragonborn broker who learned early that fear is cheaper than mercy, but stability pays better than chaos. His stone-and-mountain dragonborn lineage gives him mineral awareness, tremor-sense instincts, mountain endurance, and a lawful sentinel’s mind, making him excellent at reading both terrain and power structures before deciding who should be threatened, paid, or replaced.
In Thalryss, where piracy and registered crime can be legal if the paperwork is clean, Gavren keeps the Carnival Tribute Office running as the Nefaric Veil’s second-brain: tribute schedules, raider truces, punishment contracts, and exit plans all pass through him. He despises ichor-addled raiders who burn through profit for a stronger high, preferring disciplined brutality, useful alliances, and bosses ambitious enough to expand but not foolish enough to become targets themselves.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Geneva Clerkglass
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Geneva Clerkglass is a polished Giff city clerk whose manners are so controlled that people forget she decides who reaches the desk, the door, the warrant, and the mayor. At the Zarveng Guild Desk, she manages appointments, sealed correspondence, civic filings, and the small procedural delays that can save a life or ruin one. She is not openly cruel, but she is deeply institutional: if the truth threatens the city’s stability, Geneva will first ask whether the truth has filed the proper form.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Gloria No-Chain
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Gloria No-Chain is a fierce, blunt, combat-ready Feral Tiefling who was once treated like property and now makes it everyone’s problem when anyone else is treated the same. She is sarcastic, impatient with soft excuses, and terrifying in a fight, but her anger is rooted in loyalty: she believes escapees, constructs, Soulbounds, ichor-marked victims, and rewritten people all deserve freedom, not “proper handling.”
At the Palevanna Transit Yard, Gloria serves the Freeblade Veil as a safehouse heavy, clearing routes, escorting fugitives, and holding chokepoints when polite rescue becomes open battle. She especially hates missions that force her to destroy controlled or unfinished artificial beings, because to Gloria, even the roughest-made person deserves a chance to be more than the purpose someone built into them.

In Loxvire, he trains zealots, protects ritual sites, and leads The Choral Synod hardliners who believe divine contamination must be endured, mastered, or worshiped rather than feared. He is honorable by his own code, courteous to worthy enemies, and terrifying because he can make fanaticism sound like battlefield duty.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Grayson
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Grayson is a bold, sharp-witted Deorbasun tracker with a protective streak so strong it borders on territorial law. Cast out young and forced to survive on instinct, they now use humor, suspicion, cooking, and uncanny trail-reading to keep their chosen family fed, found, and defended.
Their Deorbasun blood makes them especially tuned to scent, movement, emotional shifts, disturbed ground, and spiritual pressure, turning them into the kind of companion who notices danger before anyone else has named it. Through the Freeblade Veil, Grayson works from the Freeblade Kennel as a loyal guide, short-order cook, spirit-sensitive scout, and defender of strays, wards, and anyone they decide belongs to the pack.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Grond of the Milk-Oath
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Grond of the Milk-Oath is a blunt, towering Goliath warrior who mistakes poetry for literal instruction and believes “kindness” must be some hidden strength mortals drink, train, or beat into themselves. As one of Anubaldir’s giantkin, they value endurance, shared burden, direct conflict, and visible strength, but their travels slowly teach them that people survive through loyalty, settlement bonds, and fighting for those weaker than themselves.
At the Settlement Training Yard, Grond serves the Crucible Wardens as a siege companion and brutal defensive instructor, teaching recruits how to hold gates, break charges, and stop panicking when larger monsters hit the wall. They are loud, literal, battle-hungry, and often alarming, but their growing fascination with “the milk of mercy” makes them unexpectedly protective of civilians, chosen family, and any settlement that proves strength means standing together.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Hannik Vox
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Hannik Vox is a theatrical, hedonistic, sharp-smiling Gwynis mayor who looks like trouble, talks like a revolutionary, and still somehow means it when they promise the unwanted will have a place to sleep. As a dream-born Gwynis, they/he carries Raeshkul and Eirzunet’s influence through memory, illusion, psychic insight, and shadowed dreamcraft, using charm and eerie perception to read a room before deciding whether it needs mercy, blackmail, or a knife.
Years ago, Hannik fled polished civic cruelty, fell into grief and black-market ichor, and deliberately took a dangerous pure dose that changed their body, slowed their aging, and made them impossible to fully separate from the vice-soaked underworld they now protects. From the Vice District Civic Hall, Hannik governs Seawynd Hollow with a loose hand and a hard line: revelry, sex work, ichor use, smuggling, and ugly survival are tolerated, but predators who threaten the district’s outcasts become public examples very quickly.

From the Solthera Watch Office, he guards doctrine, interrogates dissent, and shapes The Choral Synod policy around obedience, purity, and the useful fear of outside corruption. immersiveRosterNpcs.name: High Custodian Maxton Vale
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
High Custodian Maxton Vale is a young but severe Gnarlborn commander burdened by legacy, prophecy, and the expectation that he must become harder than the collapsing world around him. As a bark-skinned, ancient-tree people shaped by Hathruna’s cycles of rebirth, rot, roots, and living wilderness, Maxton has immense endurance and a deep instinct for preservation, but he twists that protective nature into strict control over dangerous relics, thundercoil arms, ichor-powered engines, and forbidden research.
From the Othéryn Guild Desk, Maxton leads the Crucible Wardens as a disciplined military archivist: recover what can protect settlements, lock away what can corrupt them, and destroy what no mortal institution can safely hold. He is charismatic, ruthless when afraid, genuinely protective of his people, and dangerously convinced that civilization survives only when softer hearts obey those willing to make brutal decisions; Othéryn itself sits among Gruddirynn’s villages, giving him a small frontier post from which to dream far bigger than his station.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Hollis Combe
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Hollis Combe is a tired, defensive Kithkin merchant who knows how to keep shelves stocked, ledgers balanced, and customers handled, but has grown small-hearted inside the safety of vault-and-bunker life. He was once warmer, more attentive, and genuinely helpful at the trade desk, but resentment, boredom, and a quiet dependence on diluted ichor have made him evasive, self-pitying, and prone to blaming the people closest to him for the life he helped build.
At the Caelthyrûn Guild Desk, Hollis sells household goods, vault supplies, repair kits, preserved food, and bunker necessities for the Regent Lattice, though his personal habits make him less reliable than his inventory. He is not cruel in a grand way, just disappointingly weak: the sort of man who still knows right from wrong, still occasionally does the decent thing, and still keeps choosing comfort, flirtation, and ichor-fogged avoidance over the family and community that need him awake.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Hyris Rooftreader
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Hyris Rooftreader is a lean, watchful Tabaxi courier who treats rooftops, chimneys, laundry lines, and bell towers as safer roads than anything with a gate. They move messages, ration tokens, and emergency warnings between Freeblade safehouses, preferring speed and surprise over heroic speeches. Hyris is cocky on the roofline and tender in private, especially with fugitives who freeze when freedom requires one more dangerous jump.

immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Irma Velvetglass is a Celestial Elf memory-den host who dresses grief in velvet, candlelight, perfume, and plausible deniability. She offers curated recollection rituals, dream seats, old love reenactments, and supervised ichor-adjacent memory treatments to people who can pay or who are broken enough that someone else pays for them. Irma is theatrical, warm, and business-minded, but she knows nostalgia becomes a narcotic when the present hurts too much to inhabit.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Isabel Cruzgear
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Isabel Cruzgear is a Gnome inventor whose genius curdled under isolation, grief, and the belief that a perfect machine could solve what people were too frightened to face. In Kharrowport’s transit works, she builds rescue devices, defensive constructs, and sealed mechanisms for the Regent Lattice while quietly fearing that every invention is one bad instruction away from atrocity. Isabel is not malicious, but she is proof that good intentions become monstrous when no one is allowed to question the blueprint.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Jezra Brassbite
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Jezra Brassbite is a Relicborn theorist awakened from an ancient reliquary-core, their “severed head” less a machine part and more a preserved artifact vessel full of fragmented memories, old calculations, and spiteful survival instincts. As a Setrimir-shaped artificial being, they carry the strange inheritance of stolen knowledge, awakened purpose, and relic-born consciousness, making them brilliant, rude, precise, and absolutely convinced that most living people are inefficient arrangements of panic and fluids.
At the Heth'vára Transit Yard, Jezra works with the Regent Lattice as a consultant on rogue constructs, relic systems, divine-residue logic loops, and ichor-corrupted safety protocols. They claim their brutal theories are “mercy by mathematics,” but their fixation on preventing suffering by removing choice, risk, or occasionally the patient makes them useful, terrifying, and best kept far away from unsupervised triage.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Katy Storybell
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Katy Storybell is a careful, warm, slightly anxious schoolteacher who believes education is one of the last honest tools civilization has left. She loves her students deeply, but shrinking class sizes and limited teaching materials make her quietly worry that she is preparing them for a world she herself is too cautious to face.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Keleo Briarvast
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Keleo Briarvast is calm, elegant, openly dangerous, and almost insultingly polite about how many ways she knows to end a conversation permanently. As a Firbolg, she carries Anubaldir’s quiet inheritance of hidden strength, endurance, and protective stewardship, but in Stormgullet that guardian instinct has hardened into territorial paranoia: her shop, her clients, and her secrets are all things she protects with lethal precision.
At the Velvet Armory, Keleo sells black-market blades, firearms, thundercoil weapons, warded ammunition, explosives, and discreet “problem-solving packages” to anyone with enough coin and enough nerve. Her work with the Brass Concordat makes her less a simple merchant and more a contingency planner for Virelport’s underworld, keeping private kill-ledgers on rivals, militia captains, informants, and anyone foolish enough to threaten her business while the province’s street-level corruption and transit politics keep everyone looking elsewhere.

immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Kell Orggan is an old Shadowmoor Elf mercenary whose long life has been cut into contracts, funerals, and things he survived by becoming worse than the people hunting him. He works for the Glasswell Institute because they pay, enhance, and point him at targets, but his loyalty is transactional and his conscience is buried rather than gone. Kell is quiet, brutal, and almost bored by violence until a job brushes against the few memories he has not managed to kill.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Kent Connol
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Kent Connol is a Gnome radio dramatist whose belief in masked heroes is embarrassing, contagious, and more politically dangerous than anyone expects. He writes morality plays, crime serials, and coded broadcasts for the Brass Concordat, using melodrama to remind frightened listeners that cruelty is not the same thing as strength. Kent is anxious but brave when cornered, and his stories sometimes inspire people to do the right thing before he is ready to survive the consequences.

immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Ser Dain Calvorr is a disciplined Warforged skyship paladin whose whole identity was built around order, honorable command, and the belief that dangerous relics belong under armed custody. Shawnie is a bright, anxious, endlessly curious Wechselkind child-construct who loves taking things apart, but only because they want to understand how to make them safer, kinder, or more useful. As a Wechselkind, they/he was made for adaptation and shifting function, carrying Setrimir’s influence through artificial life, awakened machinery, stolen knowledge, and the painful question of whether a built child is allowed to choose who they become.
At the Lorangriel Transit Yard, Shawnie accepts harmless errands for scrap, broken tools, clockwork bits, damaged lenses, empty vials, transit tags, and safe relic fragments, then turns them into small gifts or useful devices for the person who helped them. They/he absolutely despises Taska Thistleglimmer, not because Shawnie lacks curiosity, but because Taska keeps sending people into danger to satisfy it; to Shawnie, discovery is only worthwhile if everyone comes home with all their fingers, memories, and souls still attached. Lorangriel is the capital of El'dravire Riverrealm, giving Shawnie a major transit hub full of salvage, travelers, and Glasswell Institute oversight to quietly study.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Sheff of the Empty Cup
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Sheff of the Empty Cup is a shaky but sweet-natured Sea Elf drifter trying to rebuild their life after years of dependence on cheap diluted ichor tonics nearly ruined them. Their fixation has shifted onto Kelp-Kola, a fizzy caffeinated drink made from kelp, sugar, mineral salts, and coastal herbs, which they treat like a miracle cure, comfort object, and personal religion all at once. Sea elves in Belavadös are ocean-adapted people tied to reef culture, aquatic survival, and seafaring communities, which fits Sheff’s water-hauling work and nervous familiarity with canals, cisterns, and shoreline errands.
At the Thyravéa-Morn Guild Desk, Sheff runs water errands, carries messages, helps stock boarding houses, and rambles endlessly about Kelp-Kola flavors, bottle shapes, carbonation strength, and “proper drinking temperature.” They are awkward, lonely, overly grateful for small kindnesses, and more perceptive than people assume; the Freeblade Veil keep them close because a reliable bed, honest work, and one cold bottle can sometimes save a life better than any sermon. Thyravéa-Morn is one of Vuelmora’s towns, and Vuelmora is treated as a plains province with deep-cavern and subterranean settlement layers, giving Sheff plenty of uneasy routes, water stores, and settlement errands to navigate.

He builds pumps, beds, generators, barricades, and improvised defenses for the Freeblade Veil, treating every safe wall and warm lamp as proof that survival can become a home. immersiveRosterNpcs.description:

As an Iskareth-shaped beastfolk, he is reactive, evasive, socially alert, and driven by kinship bonds, which makes him excellent at reading customers, danger, and family trouble before anyone says the quiet part aloud.

immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Vellum Tekt is a fast-talking Satyr salesman with old-world polish, nervous charm, and the hollow-eyed exhaustion of someone who spent decades selling safety he was never allowed to receive himself. As a Thalunesh-touched Satyr, he masks trauma with jokes, brochures, rehearsed optimism, and theatrical friendliness, but every locked door and denied refuge still lives under his smile.
At the Eldryssar Clinic, Vellum now works with the Regent Lattice selling bunker berths, reinforced shelter contracts, evacuation ledgers, and “future-proof” survival packages to families afraid of divine breaches, ichor contamination, and civic collapse. He is irritating, pitiable, surprisingly useful, and desperate to matter again—especially if someone gives him a real settlement post instead of treating him like a relic from a failed sales pitch.

Satyrs are goat-legged fey known for revelry, music, and indulgence in natural pleasures. They often serve as companions of wilderness spirits and chaotic celebration. immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Veyr of Seventeen Names
immersiveRosterNpcs.description:
Veyr of Seventeen Names is charming, evasive, and almost compulsively dishonest about their own history, but their lies are usually armor wrapped around guilt rather than simple cruelty. As a Changeling shaped by Thalunesh’s influence over shapeshifters, wanderers, tricks, and misdirection, they treat identity like a tool, a weapon, and a wound all at once.
For the Freeblade Veil, Veyr works as a false-name spy out of the Freeblade Safehouse, watching docks, taverns, transit ledgers, shrine records, and faction offices for signs that someone vulnerable is about to be exposed. In Veilstrand, where Virelport’s corruption, transit politics, missing workers, and sealed divine mechanisms already make truth dangerous, Veyr specializes in moving people before the law realizes which name to arrest.

immersiveRosterNpcs.name: Will Black
immersiveRosterNpcs.description: Will Black is a Goblin Operator boss whose charm is all silk sleeves, quick numbers, and the confidence of someone born understanding that violence is easier to sell when it looks civilized. From the Rnzeuluun Clinic, he brokers tribute shares, ransom agreements, market access, and The Nefaric Veil investments while letting rougher allies look like the real monsters. He is witty, spoiled, dangerous, and clever enough to know that money can make a crime respectable before the blood dries.

npcs.name: Aaron Vaelriven
npcs.description: Aaron Vaelriven uses the warmth of a radio performer and a tailor’s patience to hide how violently his wild magic answers fear. As a half elf of Pallid Elf descent, he reads moonlit symbols, thread-signs, and ichor-stained ledgers with an intuition that frightens even him. He wants to protect Caelthir without being treated like a weapon, which makes every secret he keeps both tender and dangerous.
npcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Vaerûn-Keth is a Village in Zal’tharuun, under Tribal Confederation, with moderate danger, Beach and grass with water, Beach and reefs with water, Farming terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Half Elf reads through the Half-Elf (choose an Elf Bloodline) entry of the race compendium, within Humans, Near-Humans, and Mixed Heritage, marked by Nebyrr. Half-elves are dual-natured beings born of human and elven lineage, often balancing ambition with longevity. They tend to struggle with identity but excel at diplomacy, adaptability, and bridging cultures. Table cues: +2 Charisma, +1 to Two Other Ability Scores, Darkvision, Fey Ancestry; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Cooperative - Neutral.
rumors: Aaron Vaelriven knows why an ichor ledger changed hands last Ishtaday.
Aaron Vaelriven has a contact in Virelyss who will deny everything.
plotHooks: Aaron Vaelriven asks the party to quietly protect Caelthir after a broadcast performance causes Final Seal glyphs to appear in the studio glass.
A Melinoe-touched ichor broker offers Aaron control over his magic if he steals a sealed The Brass Concordat ledger before Caelthir can decode it.

npcs.name: Abbot Wallwhite
npcs.description: Abbot Wallwhite is a meticulous Faerie wall painter who treats civic color, public morale, and visible maintenance as matters of political survival. He restores murals, boundary marks, warning signs, and city walls for the Brass Concordat, grumbling that people notice corruption faster when the paint stops being refreshed. Abbot can seem fussy, but his eye for surface damage often catches sabotage, hidden doors, ichor seepage, and blood washed badly from stone.
npcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Vulkradûn is a City in Zharvokh, under Military Regency, with high danger, Beach and grass with water, Farming, Partial forest terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Faerie reads through the Fey-Folk entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Fey-Folk are peoples shaped by glamour, luck, tiny or otherworldly bodies, dreamlike emotion, and trickster magic. At my table, Faerie, Fairy, and Gandirosha are not separate top-level races here; they are bloodlines. Table cues: Fey Creature Type or Fey Ancestry, Fey Magic, Glamour or Luck Expression, Small/Tiny Fey Presence; starting tendency Neutral - Chaotic - Cooperative - Neutral.
rumors: Abbot can identify three kinds of ichor leakage by how primer refuses to dry over them.
He once insulted a mayor's entire administration by repainting one wall exactly the color it had been before the scandal.
plotHooks: Abbot asks the party to guard a wall restoration after finding a message bleeding through seven layers of paint.
A civic mural begins changing overnight, showing crimes the watch has not yet discovered.
End of organized NPC roster.

npcs.name: Adamma Gearmourne
npcs.description:
Adamma Gearmourne is a precise, grief-tempered Autognome built for repair, defense, salvage, and caravan protection, but loss has sharpened their purpose into something closer to vengeance. As an Autognome shaped by Marduthor’s craft, machinery, architecture, and underground-hall traditions, they are lawful, resilient, tool-minded, and prone to processing emotion through maintenance routines, battle modifications, and carefully itemized revenge lists.
From the Regent Lattice Repair Bay in Pellavess, Adamma works with the Regent Lattice to repair damaged constructs, salvage broken automata, reinforce traveling crews, and hunt rogue clockworks that threaten trade routes. They speak with controlled courtesy, but beneath it is a deep mourning for the caravan-family they lost, and they sometimes wonder whether feeling pain makes them more alive or merely more breakable.
npcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Pellavess is a Village in Nalvessir, under Communalism, with low danger, Farming, Partial forest, Mountain range terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Autognome reads through the Autognome entry of the race compendium, within Constructed and Artificial Beings, marked by Setrimir. Autognomes are mechanical or magically animated constructs resembling gnomes. They are often designed for specific purposes and may develop emergent personality traits over time. Table cues: Construct, Armored Casing, Built for Success, Healing Machine; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Cooperative - Honorable.

npcs.name: Agent Xevran Gostamin
npcs.description:
Agent Xevran Gostamin is precise, intimidating, and emotionally sealed behind professional discipline, treating every assignment like a matter of containment rather than cruelty. As a Jazwed Dragonborn, xe carries lava-and-crystal lineage traits tied to fire, stone, elemental shaping, defensive engineering, and lawful enforcement, making xem terrifyingly suited to pursuit, extraction, and controlled violence.
From the Directorate Retrieval Office, Xevran works as a hidden Glasswell Institute agent in Vaelshore, a Marrowynd town within an ocean province shaped by floating settlements and submarine access. Xe retrieves defectors, stolen research, escaped assets, fugitive witnesses, and compromised ledger-bearers with cold efficiency, but xem’s rigid loyalty can crack when a target proves more person than property.

Dragonborn are draconic humanoids born of ancient dragon lineage, elemental force, dynastic memory, and divine sovereignty. npcs.name: Archivist Thiblee Jannar
npcs.description:
Archivist Thiblee Jannar is a brilliant, anxious Tiefling lore-proctor with a talent for arcane systems, construct interfaces, archive wards, and accidentally activating exactly the wrong failsafe at the worst possible time. He/them is socially awkward, over-eager, and sometimes oblivious to how dangerous his curiosity can become, but his intelligence is real, especially when repairing sentient machinery, decoding relic protocols, or building safer ways to catalogue ichor-tainted artifacts.
At the Kael'vyrûn Market Hall, Thiblee works for the Crucible Wardens maintaining relic inventories, automated archive assistants, restricted research ledgers, and containment records for ichor-powered devices. He is deeply devoted to his spouse, Scribe Paelyn Jannar, who helps keep him grounded when ambition, insecurity, or a very tempting glowing button threatens to turn “one quick upgrade” into a citywide emergency.

Tiefling reads through the Tiefling entry of the race compendium, within Celestial, Fiendish, and Planar Bloodlines, marked by Freyseth. Tieflings are fiend-touched humanoids marked by infernal ancestry and social stigma. They often develop strong individuality and resilience in the face of prejudice. Table cues: Darkvision, Fiendish Legacy, Otherworldly Presence; starting tendency Neutral - Chaotic - Neutral - Neutral.

npcs.name: Barney Rook
npcs.description: Barney Rook is a cranky Hederan retired marksman who has turned the Pokbith Archive into a half-library, half-firing nest, and he insists both functions are equally educational. Age has not softened his eye or his temper; he still names favored weapons, lectures strangers about sightlines, and treats every broken turret like a neglected old soldier. The Brass Concordat keeps him close because he knows how old defenses fail, how monsters breach them, and which official records lied about both.

Hederan reads through the Hederan entry of the race compendium, within Primitive, Tribal, and Wilderness Humanoids, marked by Asethyr. Wilderness-bound survivalists adapted to harsh biomes through ritualized instinct and ancestral knowledge. They thrive in isolation but maintain strong clan bonds. npcs.name: Bertha Smallreed
npcs.description: Bertha Smallreed is a young Halfling organizer with more courage than most adults around her and very little patience for being told to wait until things get worse. In Greenhollow Plains, she pushes the Choral Synod, local workers, and frightened families to repair defenses, share supplies, and stop pretending children do not notice political cowardice. She is charming, stubborn, and dangerous to complacent officials because she asks simple questions they cannot answer without admitting guilt.

npcs.description:
Brew-Bell Buddy is a cheerful Autognome brewing construct built to chill, carbonate, ferment, and dispense tavern drinks while telling terrible jokes at exactly the wrong time. As a Marduthor-shaped machine-soul, they treat recipes like sacred engineering, carefully balancing kelp ales, root fizz, mineral tonics, and legally diluted ichor cordials so travelers get comfort without being quietly poisoned.

They are friendly, literal, surprisingly durable in a fight, and deeply attached to anyone who treats them as a person rather than a walking keg with warranty violations.

npcs.description:
Caetha Redglass is furious, sharp-tongued, hard to comfort, and even harder to fool, but her cruelty is mostly scar tissue from a life where every offer of kindness came with a hook in it. As a Half-Orc, she carries Nebyrr’s mixed-heritage pull toward survival, structure, and principled endurance, twisted by betrayal into a belief that deals are safer than love and violence is more honest than sympathy.
At the Red Pit Bathhouse, Caetha fights because pain is familiar, coin is clean, and the crowd’s roar is easier to trust than quiet concern. Her long-term addiction is to battle-grade ichor—especially the black-market, rage-bright kind used by pit crews and desperate duelists—and the Brass Concordat sees her as both a dangerous asset and a living witness to how Eldermere’s polished civic order still profits from broken people.

She is warm in public, exhausted in private, and ruthless when a community’s survival demands that someone give the order no one else wants to own.

npcs.description:
Captain Kellis Vorn is a severe, disciplined Noitzideq Dragonborn skyship captain who believes order is not a preference but the only thing keeping dangerous relics, ichor-fueled engines, and foolish recruits from burning half the province out of the sky. Shaped by Valkhamesh’s draconic inheritance and Iazethas’ harsh culture of law, sovereignty, and military duty, he respects chain of command, clean logistics, decisive elimination of threats, and officers who prove themselves through results rather than speeches.
At the Streccea Guild Desk, Kellis commands Crucible Custodian air operations: skyship patrols, relic-retrieval drops, squire training flights, contraband sweeps, and high-risk strikes against factions trafficking unstable ichor technology. He is loyal to Maxton Vale’s larger mission, but not blindly sentimental about it; if an asset, ally, or escaped experiment threatens civilian safety or Custodian secrecy, Kellis will mark the target and expect the job done cleanly.

npcs.description:
Chirra Clickspring is a sharp-eyed, fast-talking caravan merchant whose cheer comes in sparks: bright, jittery, funny, and always a little too close to panic. As a Gandirosha, fae has a natural feel for luck, hidden danger, loaded bargains, false smiles, and the tiny social openings that let a merchant survive roads full of monsters, debt collectors, and armed customers.

Publicly, Chirra is a The Brass Concordat trader out of Qasvire in Bravelyn; secretly, fae sells route gossip, fugitive sightings, and suspicious traveler names to whoever pays enough, then laughs too loudly when accused of having a conscience.

npcs.description: Cog Vell is a precise, anxious Monodrone merchant with a clockmaker’s patience, a survivalist’s caution, and the exhausted humor of someone who has spent too long pretending not to care. They keep their shelves neat, their ledgers exact, and their emotions compartmentalized, but their ward-like loyalty to memory-wounded refugees makes it obvious that their detachment is more shield than truth. npcs.name: Cogsworth Brasswell
npcs.description: Cogsworth Brasswell is a polished, fussy, heartbreakingly loyal Warforged steward built for domestic care, household order, childcare, gardening, and ceremonial hospitality. As one of Setrimir’s awakened constructs, he clings to routine because routine is how he proves love: every swept hall, mended kettle, trimmed hedge, and warmed hearth becomes an act of devotion rather than mere programming. Beneath his bright manners and brass-button propriety is a lonely, anxious soul terrified that the people he cares for may never come home, so he pretends the household can still be saved if he simply keeps everything ready. In Bronzewake, he serves with the Freeblade Veil, restoring abandoned homes and ruined family estates for refugees, heirs, debtors, and displaced households. His work at the Old Household Manse makes him part steward, part caretaker, part grief counselor, and part walking emergency protocol for families trying to rebuild in Virelport’s capital.

npcs.description:
Cyrille Bellwisp is unfailingly polite, curious, gentle, and clinically fearless, with a scholar’s delight in dreadful things that makes them seem naïve even when she is standing in the middle of horror. As a Geppettin, Cyrille is one of Setrimir’s constructed peoples: artisan-crafted, socially expressive, purpose-built for specialized labor, and shaped by the strange dignity of artificial life trying to become more than its original function.
At the Ichor-Regulated Medical Office, Cyrille studies infection, divine residue, addiction damage, black-market ichor poisoning, and long-term exposure to contaminated god-prison byproducts. Their work with the Regent Lattice makes her a physician, archivist, and sealed-laboratory custodian in Lithvar’s underdeep medical network, where she is eager to help patients but sometimes dangerously slow to recognize when “valuable research” began as someone else’s cruelty.

npcs.description: Daisy Ashpetal is a Reborn bookseller with old grief in her bones and a shop full of maps, ration guides, children's primers, banned memoirs, and things she insists are not sentimental. She has survived enough eras to know the difference between danger and loneliness, so she quietly helps mercenaries, refugees, and investigators find leads when official channels have failed them. Daisy is dry, kind, and impossible to impress, but she remembers every person who tried to become better and every city that punished them for it.

npcs.description: Dan Honesthand is a Dara contract investigator with a plainspoken manner, sharp eyes, and a stubborn hatred of staged evidence. He follows missing caravan claims, suspicious settlements, forged rescue stories, and ichor-tainted testimony for the Brass Concordat, trusting facts more than charm. Dan is not gentle, but he is fair, and that makes him dangerous in towns where everyone has agreed to survive by lying together.

npcs.description: Dara Hubbell is a Star Elf cult leader whose faith in the heavens sounds ridiculous until her followers start producing maps, omens, and ritual mathematics that should not work. From the Abyrros Tavern, she leads a small star-seeking movement inside the Nefaric Veil, offering initiation, cosmic explanations, and expensive routes toward promised transcendence. She is earnest, manipulative, visionary, and never entirely easy to dismiss, especially under a sky where the Star-River answers back.

At the Leammipa Tavern, she sells blades, thundercoil parts, ammunition, armor plates, and practical advice through the Brass Concordat, refusing to romanticize violence while profiting from everyone else’s fear of it. npcs.description: Dejen Saltglass is a small, sharp-tongued Halfling arms merchant who survives by being cleverer than the people who underestimate him and meaner than the people who pity him. He claims he does not need friends, but his suspicion comes from having watched safehouses fall, escape routes burn, and “trusted” protectors sell vulnerable people back into cages. At the Vorthélyn Archive, Dejen sells weapons, ammunition, fog-safe armor, emergency supplies, and controlled anti-ichor remedies through the Choral Synod, always watching for infiltrators, retrieval agents, and anyone asking too many gentle questions. He is bitter, witty, strategic, and difficult to comfort, but beneath the insults is a fiercely practical defender of refugees who believes survival depends on secrecy, leverage, and never letting enemies decide when mercy is convenient.

npcs.name: Desmera Veil
npcs.description:
Desmera Veil is a cautious, steel-spined Mycelian organizer who asks one question before trusting anyone: whether they would risk themselves for a person the law has already decided is property, evidence, or waste. As a Mycelian, she is tied to vast underground fungal memory-networks, making her a living archive of routes, disappearances, betrayals, and safe names, with Hathruna’s influence showing through decay, renewal, roots, fungi, and communal survival.
From the Blacktide Reach Guild Desk, Desmera leads the Freeblade Veil as a lantern-mother, coordinating coded signs, safehouses, dead drops, forged identities, and emergency extractions through Marrowynd’s floating and submarine-linked settlements. She is warm only after proof, ruthless when secrecy breaks, and deeply opposed to ichor-fueled institutions that treat sentient people as assets to harvest, reset, sell, or reclaim.

She keeps Glasswell Institute power systems, transit engines, and ichor-processing conduits functioning through stubborn craft, ruthless prioritization, and a terrifying memory for who ignored her warnings. npcs.description: Dr. Amara Mneme is a Kenku memory surgeon who speaks softly, listens brutally, and knows that the mind can be both evidence and crime scene. At the Brass Concordat, she guides patients through memory dives, trauma echoes, stolen identities, and ichor-damaged recollections, using repeated phrases and mirrored voices to anchor people who might otherwise vanish inside themselves. Amara is compassionate but not sentimental; she will open a memory like a wound if truth is the only way to save the living.

npcs.description:
Dr. Andera Sootvein is a blunt, road-tested Dwarf physician with steady hands, a soot-black sense of humor, and very little patience for patients who lie about what they drank, injected, inhaled, or bought from “a perfectly reputable cousin.” As a Marduthor-shaped Dwarf, they/she approaches medicine like craftwork: diagnose the crack, brace the structure, drain the poison, repair what can be repaired, and tell the fool exactly how close they came to dying.
At the Soltharyn Basin Tavern, Andera runs a back-room surgery center for wounds, curse-sickness, divine residue exposure, and ichor addiction, including withdrawal from diluted shop tonics, black-market battle ichor, and tavern-brewed “miracle” mixtures. The Brass Concordat values them because they can tell the difference between ordinary illness, bad liquor, contaminated ichor, and someone quietly being used as evidence in a larger crime.

He patches Freeblade agents, removes ichor-trace brands, keeps fugitives alive after botched extractions, and never lets gratitude distract him from asking who compromised the safehouse. Carris is principled, skeptical, and exhausting; he believes mercy without operational discipline only creates more bodies for someone else to bury.

Clay is charming, remote, and dangerous because he can make exploitation sound like patience with a long enough research timeline.

Justen is not reckless; he is methodical, vindictive, and convinced that the world is safer when people are too afraid to run.

npcs.description:
Elder Lorn Fogfellow is a bitter, weather-beaten Rainforest Dril’thar guide who knows every drowned trail, fog-choked root bridge, and monster path around Syl'thara. As a Dril’thar, he carries Bastveig’s living-water memory and the rainforest line’s Sigrananna influence, making him a natural hunter, navigator, and keeper of grief-soaked places where water remembers the dead.

Gavren Portlock is a hard-eyed, practical Tuorszom Dragonborn broker who learned early that fear is cheaper than mercy, but stability pays better than chaos. His stone-and-mountain dragonborn lineage gives him mineral awareness, tremor-sense instincts, mountain endurance, and a lawful sentinel’s mind, making him excellent at reading both terrain and power structures before deciding who should be threatened, paid, or replaced.

He despises ichor-addled raiders who burn through profit for a stronger high, preferring disciplined brutality, useful alliances, and bosses ambitious enough to expand but not foolish enough to become targets themselves.

Gloria No-Chain is a fierce, blunt, combat-ready Feral Tiefling who was once treated like property and now makes it everyone’s problem when anyone else is treated the same. She is sarcastic, impatient with soft excuses, and terrifying in a fight, but her anger is rooted in loyalty: she believes escapees, constructs, Soulbounds, ichor-marked victims, and rewritten people all deserve freedom, not “proper handling.”
At the Palevanna Transit Yard, Gloria serves the Freeblade Veil as a safehouse heavy, clearing routes, escorting fugitives, and holding chokepoints when polite rescue becomes open battle. npcs.name: Grond of the Milk-Oath
npcs.description:
Grond of the Milk-Oath is a blunt, towering Goliath warrior who mistakes poetry for literal instruction and believes “kindness” must be some hidden strength mortals drink, train, or beat into themselves. As one of Anubaldir’s giantkin, they value endurance, shared burden, direct conflict, and visible strength, but their travels slowly teach them that people survive through loyalty, settlement bonds, and fighting for those weaker than themselves.
At the Settlement Training Yard, Grond serves the Crucible Wardens as a siege companion and brutal defensive instructor, teaching recruits how to hold gates, break charges, and stop panicking when larger monsters hit the wall. They are loud, literal, battle-hungry, and often alarming, but their growing fascination with “the milk of mercy” makes them unexpectedly protective of civilians, chosen family, and any settlement that proves strength means standing together.

npcs.name: Hannik Vox
npcs.description:
Hannik Vox is a theatrical, hedonistic, sharp-smiling Gwynis mayor who looks like trouble, talks like a revolutionary, and still somehow means it when they promise the unwanted will have a place to sleep. As a dream-born Gwynis, they/he carries Raeshkul and Eirzunet’s influence through memory, illusion, psychic insight, and shadowed dreamcraft, using charm and eerie perception to read a room before deciding whether it needs mercy, blackmail, or a knife.
Years ago, Hannik fled polished civic cruelty, fell into grief and black-market ichor, and deliberately took a dangerous pure dose that changed their body, slowed their aging, and made them impossible to fully separate from the vice-soaked underworld they now protects. From the Vice District Civic Hall, Hannik governs Seawynd Hollow with a loose hand and a hard line: revelry, sex work, ichor use, smuggling, and ugly survival are tolerated, but predators who threaten the district’s outcasts become public examples very quickly.

npcs.description: High Confessor Tektus is a Half-Orc confessor with a sermon voice like a locked gate and a talent for turning doubt into treason. From the Solthera Watch Office, he guards doctrine, interrogates dissent, and shapes The Choral Synod policy around obedience, purity, and the useful fear of outside corruption. He is charismatic, insecure, authoritarian, and far more dangerous when he smiles than when he threatens.

npcs.name: High Custodian Maxton Vale
npcs.description:
High Custodian Maxton Vale is a young but severe Gnarlborn commander burdened by legacy, prophecy, and the expectation that he must become harder than the collapsing world around him. As a bark-skinned, ancient-tree people shaped by Hathruna’s cycles of rebirth, rot, roots, and living wilderness, Maxton has immense endurance and a deep instinct for preservation, but he twists that protective nature into strict control over dangerous relics, thundercoil arms, ichor-powered engines, and forbidden research.
From the Othéryn Guild Desk, Maxton leads the Crucible Wardens as a disciplined military archivist: recover what can protect settlements, lock away what can corrupt them, and destroy what no mortal institution can safely hold. He is charismatic, ruthless when afraid, genuinely protective of his people, and dangerously convinced that civilization survives only when softer hearts obey those willing to make brutal decisions; Othéryn itself sits among Gruddirynn’s villages, giving him a small frontier post from which to dream far bigger than his station.

npcs.name: Hollis Combe
npcs.description:
Hollis Combe is a tired, defensive Kithkin merchant who knows how to keep shelves stocked, ledgers balanced, and customers handled, but has grown small-hearted inside the safety of vault-and-bunker life. He was once warmer, more attentive, and genuinely helpful at the trade desk, but resentment, boredom, and a quiet dependence on diluted ichor have made him evasive, self-pitying, and prone to blaming the people closest to him for the life he helped build.
At the Caelthyrûn Guild Desk, Hollis sells household goods, vault supplies, repair kits, preserved food, and bunker necessities for the Regent Lattice, though his personal habits make him less reliable than his inventory. He is not cruel in a grand way, just disappointingly weak: the sort of man who still knows right from wrong, still occasionally does the decent thing, and still keeps choosing comfort, flirtation, and ichor-fogged avoidance over the family and community that need him awake.

npcs.description: Hyris Rooftreader is a lean, watchful Tabaxi courier who treats rooftops, chimneys, laundry lines, and bell towers as safer roads than anything with a gate. They move messages, ration tokens, and emergency warnings between Freeblade safehouses, preferring speed and surprise over heroic speeches. Hyris is cocky on the roofline and tender in private, especially with fugitives who freeze when freedom requires one more dangerous jump.

npcs.description: Irma Velvetglass is a Celestial Elf memory-den host who dresses grief in velvet, candlelight, perfume, and plausible deniability. She offers curated recollection rituals, dream seats, old love reenactments, and supervised ichor-adjacent memory treatments to people who can pay or who are broken enough that someone else pays for them. Irma is theatrical, warm, and business-minded, but she knows nostalgia becomes a narcotic when the present hurts too much to inhabit.

npcs.name: Isabel Cruzgear
npcs.description: Isabel Cruzgear is a Gnome inventor whose genius curdled under isolation, grief, and the belief that a perfect machine could solve what people were too frightened to face. In Kharrowport’s transit works, she builds rescue devices, defensive constructs, and sealed mechanisms for the Regent Lattice while quietly fearing that every invention is one bad instruction away from atrocity. Isabel is not malicious, but she is proof that good intentions become monstrous when no one is allowed to question the blueprint.

npcs.description: Jakk Cabot is a Verdan noble scholar whose charm, wealth, and academic curiosity orbit one terrible family secret. npcs.name: Jezra Brassbite
npcs.description:
Jezra Brassbite is a Relicborn theorist awakened from an ancient reliquary-core, their “severed head” less a machine part and more a preserved artifact vessel full of fragmented memories, old calculations, and spiteful survival instincts. As a Setrimir-shaped artificial being, they carry the strange inheritance of stolen knowledge, awakened purpose, and relic-born consciousness, making them brilliant, rude, precise, and absolutely convinced that most living people are inefficient arrangements of panic and fluids.
At the Heth'vára Transit Yard, Jezra works with the Regent Lattice as a consultant on rogue constructs, relic systems, divine-residue logic loops, and ichor-corrupted safety protocols. They claim their brutal theories are “mercy by mathematics,” but their fixation on preventing suffering by removing choice, risk, or occasionally the patient makes them useful, terrifying, and best kept far away from unsupervised triage.

npcs.description: Jun Longvale is a Simic Hybrid settler moving through grief so quietly that people sometimes forget silence can be an emergency. npcs.name: Kasumi Nakren
npcs.description: Kasumi Nakren is a Kender runaway tinkerer whose curiosity is tangled with fear that her memories, body, or family story may not be entirely her own. She fled to Lunethryl chasing answers about identity, constructed life, and hidden communities, but her bravery is still the bravery of someone young enough to mistake danger for proof. The Choral Synod sees her as a vulnerable witness and a brilliant little engineer; she sees herself as a question no adult has answered honestly.

npcs.description: Katy Storybell is a careful, warm, slightly anxious schoolteacher who believes education is one of the last honest tools civilization has left. As a Half-Elf shaped by Nebyrr’s influence toward lineage, civic order, and cultural bridging, she teaches children practical literacy, local history, safety skills, moral reasoning, and the expectations of settlement life. She loves her students deeply, but shrinking class sizes and limited teaching materials make her quietly worry that she is preparing them for a world she herself is too cautious to face.

npcs.name: Keleo Briarvast
npcs.description:
Keleo Briarvast is calm, elegant, openly dangerous, and almost insultingly polite about how many ways she knows to end a conversation permanently. As a Firbolg, she carries Anubaldir’s quiet inheritance of hidden strength, endurance, and protective stewardship, but in Stormgullet that guardian instinct has hardened into territorial paranoia: her shop, her clients, and her secrets are all things she protects with lethal precision.
At the Velvet Armory, Keleo sells black-market blades, firearms, thundercoil weapons, warded ammunition, explosives, and discreet “problem-solving packages” to anyone with enough coin and enough nerve. Her work with the Brass Concordat makes her less a simple merchant and more a contingency planner for Virelport’s underworld, keeping private kill-ledgers on rivals, militia captains, informants, and anyone foolish enough to threaten her business while the province’s street-level corruption and transit politics keep everyone looking elsewhere.

npcs.name: Kell Orggan
npcs.description: Kell Orggan is an old Shadowmoor Elf mercenary whose long life has been cut into contracts, funerals, and things he survived by becoming worse than the people hunting him. He works for the Glasswell Institute because they pay, enhance, and point him at targets, but his loyalty is transactional and his conscience is buried rather than gone. Kell is quiet, brutal, and almost bored by violence until a job brushes against the few memories he has not managed to kill.

npcs.name: Kent Connol
npcs.description: Kent Connol is a Gnome radio dramatist whose belief in masked heroes is embarrassing, contagious, and more politically dangerous than anyone expects. He writes morality plays, crime serials, and coded broadcasts for the Brass Concordat, using melodrama to remind frightened listeners that cruelty is not the same thing as strength. Kent is anxious but brave when cornered, and his stories sometimes inspire people to do the right thing before he is ready to survive the consequences.

npcs.name: Kessler Gate
npcs.description: Kessler Gate is a practical Laneshi caravan mayor who keeps Oryndea moving through favors, tolls, quiet threats, and the kind of smile that means she has already counted the exits. The Brass Concordat trusts her because she understands that trade hubs survive on neutrality, controlled gossip, and hard decisions made before raiders, zealots, or hungry officials arrive. She is protective of caravan folk and refugees, but she will absolutely bury a scandal if exposing it would collapse the market that feeds them.

npcs.name: Knight Swyn Vantaufo
npcs.description:
Knight Swyn Vantaufo is a razor-tongued Dhampir watch knight with impeccable taste, lethal patience, and absolutely no interest in pretending to be nicer than she is. She is loyal with terrifying intensity once someone has earned his devotion, but strangers usually meet the cold ledger first: sarcastic, dismissive, judgmental, and very willing to remind people that politeness is optional but survival is not.
At the Neruvéa Archive, Swyn serves the Crucible Wardens as a night-watch enforcer, relic guard, and field interrogator for cases involving blood rites, undead contracts, ichor trafficking, and forbidden inheritance records. She has the old instincts of a predator and the discipline of a soldier, but his sharpest edge comes from contempt for weakness, hypocrisy, and anyone who mistakes glamour, beauty, or vice-district polish for softness.

npcs.name: Larionie Horrin
npcs.description:
Larionie Horrin is a brilliant, flirtatious, dangerous Half-Orc inventor whose charm can feel like a performance until her grief, guilt, and impossible intelligence cut through the mask. She dislikes crude violence but loves elegant solutions, so her weapons stock favors thundercoil stunners, grappler rigs, restraint devices, archive-safe explosives, and ichor-reactive tools designed to disable, contain, or outthink a threat rather than simply butcher it.
At the Yltharien Archive, Larionie works through the Brass Concordat as a specialist merchant for relic-hunters, caravan guards, and investigators who need equipment that can survive cursed ruins, divine residue, and black-market ichor contamination. She is seductive, calculating, remorseful, and capable of long, devastating plans, but she is also someone desperately trying to prove that invention can still save lives after once using genius to nearly destroy her own.

Marcea is difficult because she is wounded, not because she is empty; there is still love under the ash, but it bites anyone reaching for it too quickly.

npcs.description: Nessa Crashborn is a sharp-clawed Kobold salvage leader who treats every wreck, collapsed skyship, and broken cargo hold like a crime scene with treasure buried under the bones. Fae is guarded, territorial, and slow to trust, shaped by a burned past, a ruined family line, and the hard lesson that greed can turn a home into ashes faster than fire. Nikol Vellum is a dry, principled Relicborn detective with a battered coat, a sharper mind than most magistrates, and the uncomfortable habit of treating every missing person as if the world itself owes them an answer. As one of Setrimir’s artificial lineages, they/he carries fragmented histories inside their body, leaving them caught between borrowed memory, awakened purpose, and the stubborn choice to become more than the relic they were made from.

They/he is snarky, compassionate, self-loathing in quiet moments, and fiercely protective of anyone treated like a thing instead of a person.

npcs.name: Ozvald the Outrageous
npcs.description: Ozvald the Outrageous is a Hexblood stage mage trapped between performance, tragedy, and the desperate belief that the show must protect what is left of his people. At the Thalavaryn Workshop, he maintains illusions, stage wards, carnival horrors, and theatrical defenses for the Nefaric Veil while trying to keep cursed performers from being exterminated as monsters. npcs.name: Pammora Loom
npcs.description: Pammora Loom is a calm, unnerving Golynn oracle who speaks in probability threads instead of prophecy, mapping danger through repeated names, train delays, ration shortages, and ichor purchase patterns. The Freeblade Veil relies on them to predict raids before agents have evidence, though their warnings often sound absurd until the ambush happens exactly where they said it would. Pammora is gentle with frightened people and merciless with bad data.

npcs.name: Perrin Hearthvale
npcs.description:
Perrin Hearthvale is a weary but steadfast Centaur marshal who still believes settlements survive only when ordinary people answer one another’s calls for help. As an Asethyr-shaped Centaur, he values freedom, herd-unity, open roads, and honorable defense, but the losses he has survived have left him terrified of formal leadership even while he keeps becoming the person others follow.
In Thornbreak, one of Kharvathen’s mountain towns, Perrin works from the Freeblade Notice Hall coordinating rescue calls, militia watches, refugee escorts, and settlement defense requests. He is humble, guilt-ridden, quietly brave, and fiercely opposed to raider logic, corrupt mercenary contracts, and any “practical” plan that sacrifices civilians for convenience.

npcs.name: Piera Wrightquill
npcs.description:
Piera Wrightquill is a relentless lunar elf reporter with a talent for turning rumor, ledgers, overheard threats, and inconvenient witnesses into public scandal. Her moonlit elven instincts make her curious, adaptable, and difficult to intimidate, while Sigrananna’s influence gives her a sharp hunter’s patience when stalking a corrupt official through paper trails instead of forests.
In Cyr'ethael, a town in dragon-ruled Iazethas, Piera’s broadsheets regularly challenge draconic law, civic silence, price-fixing, poisoned canals, militia corruption, and anyone powerful enough to think truth should stay buried. She is sarcastic, lonely, brave to the point of recklessness, and deeply protective of her household, using the Public Broadsheet Office and the Brass Concordat to expose rot before it becomes accepted law.

npcs.name: Proctor Ingra Vell
npcs.description:
Proctor Ingra Vell is a sharp, sarcastic Volsarii forge-proctor with a mercenary’s practicality, a death-guide’s instincts, and a frightening talent for making people doubt themselves before a fight even begins. As one of the four-armed soul-ferriers shaped by Nefarokir, Nebyrr, and Sokhivar, she can sense fear clinging to the dead, read the emotional residue of battlefield remains, and treat fallen warriors with reverence even when she hated them alive.
At the Yire’thaulor Clinic, Ingra forges, repairs, and blesses Crucible Custodian arms used for retrieval work, battlefield containment, and the handling of ichor-tainted relics. She is rude, loyal, flirtatious when it serves her, and deeply haunted by old contracts; her cruelty is usually armor, but her sense of duty toward the dead is real enough that even her enemies get proper rites.
