npcs.name: Pykeman Redgallery
npcs.description: Pykeman Redgallery is a Verdan painter whose refined manners, crimson canvases, and selective violence make polite society unsure whether to condemn him or commission him. He targets predators, raiders, and people he considers worse than monsters, turning their deaths into warnings disguised as art. Pykeman is not safe, not sane in any simple way, and not entirely wrong about the hypocrisy of officials who object to murder only when it is aesthetically difficult to ignore.

npcs.name: Quartermaster Teagren
npcs.description:
Quartermaster Teagren is a practical, smooth-talking Gandirosha supply proctor who knows starvation kills soldiers just as surely as monsters, bad orders, or unstable relics. His luck-touched people are shaped by Thalunesh and Asethyr through charm, timing, revelry, wanderer instincts, and subtle survival magic, which makes him excellent at finding spare ammunition, hidden stores, discounted armor, and the one caravan driver willing to make a dangerous run for the right price.
At the Thornbreak Tavern, Teagren manages Crucible Custodian arms, armor, food stores, thundercoil parts, siege supplies, and questionable “off-ledger” procurement deals that keep patrols alive when official channels fail. He is friendly, mercenary, and morally flexible about sourcing crops, fuel, and diluted ichor medicine, but he is not careless: pure black-market ichor, wasteful commanders, and preventable hunger all offend him because every shortage eventually becomes a body count.

npcs.name: Ronna Shaw
npcs.description:
Ronna Shaw is a gruff, battle-seasoned Dwarf quartermaster who has seen too many bright causes ruined by fools with titles and no spine. As a Marduthor-shaped Dwarf, she respects craft, fortification, artillery, logistics, and practical defense far more than speeches, and she will not follow anyone until they prove they can protect people when the walls shake.
At the Aelgrove Guild Desk, Ronna maintains the Freeblade Veil’ heavy stores: thundercoil muskets, siege charges, artillery plans, signal flares, defensive emplacements, and the old guns nobody younger than her knows how to wake properly. She is sharp-tongued, loyal once earned, unimpressed by rank, and deeply hostile toward any faction that hoards weapons or engineering knowledge while settlements are left to die without proper defenses.

npcs.name: Rook MacReady
npcs.description:
Rook MacReady is a dry, guarded Minotaur scout with a practiced mercenary’s eye, a parent’s desperation, and a code of restraint he clings to harder than he admits. As an Anubaldir-shaped Minotaur, he carries endurance, instinctual navigation, stubborn honor, and relentless pursuit in his bones, making him ideal for long-range scouting, caravan overwatch, and finding safe routes through bad country.
He works contracts through the Caravan Contract Desk in Utch’myrith, taking dangerous jobs across Jor’maelis so he can send coin home to the sibling caring for his sick child. Rook is sarcastic, careful with violence, and ashamed of some past contracts, but every shot he takes now is measured against one question: whether it gets him closer to a cure without turning him back into the kind of hired killer his child should never have to know.

npcs.name: Roz
npcs.description: Roz is a slow-moving, slug-shaped Oozekin clerk with brownish-yellow translucence, gray eyes, a stiff crest of pale hair-like slime, black cat-eye spectacles, and a maroon vest burdened with seals, stamps, warrants, fee slips, contraband tags, and emergency ink. She lives in Leviamor, where the tide smells like brine, ink, old copper, and plausible deniability, and she serves at the Sub-33 Counter of the Thalryss Legal Cover Office. Every theft, fraud, duel, poisoning, burglary, blackmail, disappearance, inheritance correction, hostile acquisition, counterfeit relic transfer, and emotionally necessary arson in her district must pass through her desk before it becomes legal. Roz does not decide whether something is moral. Roz decides whether it was filed correctly. Inside the Black-Maw Myriad, she has begun collecting permits signed by dead applicants, impossible dates, genuine seals, and filing fees paid by people already buried, drowned, burned, eaten, dissolved, or legally absent.

npcs.description: Rufin Rubens is a Dwarf repairman with nimble hands, tavern gossip, and a talent for finding uses for machines everyone else left rusting in basements. He fixes locks, boilers, drink lines, lift gears, caravan carts, and temperamental constructs for the Brass Concordat, usually while pretending the job is easier than it is. Rufin is practical and friendly, but when old machines are tied to ichor, alcohol, or missing people, he starts asking questions no one hired him to ask.

npcs.name: Rylee Brassroad
npcs.description:
Rylee Brassroad is a restless Ombrask trade broker who left protected vault-life because safety started feeling too much like a cage. Her shadow-born nature makes her private, perceptive, and hard to pin down, with Eirzunet’s influence showing in her talent for secrecy, illusion, twilight movement, and noticing when a “perfectly legal” shipment is hiding something rotten.
At the Thal’zuroth Watch Office, Rylee works with the Brass Concordat to inspect contracts, broker trading-emporium stock, and confront suppliers whose goods are poisoning customers or masking black-market ichor contamination. She is practical, suspicious, quietly brave, and eager for a larger life, but she still carries the wary habits of someone who knows that sheltered communities can hide corruption just as easily as open roads can. Thal’zuroth is one of Zal’tharuun’s cities, and the province’s mountain underlayers make her trade routes especially tangled with cavern markets, hidden courts, and dangerous supply politics.

Local records favor Neutral, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Triton, Merfolk, Locathah, Tamhiogal, Dril'thar — Ocean. Ombrask reads through the Ombrask entry of the race compendium, within Shadow, Umbral, and Darkness-Aligned Peoples, marked by Eirzunet. Shadow-bodied beings that exist partially outside physical reality, appearing as shifting silhouettes. They are natural infiltrators who thrive in secrecy and illusion. npcs.name: Scribe Paelyn Jannar
npcs.description:
Scribe Paelyn Jannar is a brilliant, excitable Tiefling field scribe with a mind built for impossible engineering, skyship math, aetheric propulsion, and the terrifying sentence, “That should not be possible, which means it is extremely interesting.” They/her is awkward, curious, optimistic, and far braver than she looks, especially when an ichor-powered device, broken relic engine, or unstable simulation lattice threatens to erase someone from reality.
At the Élarwyn Guild Desk, Paelyn documents Crucible field tests, failed prototypes, launch calculations, memory-lattice incidents, and dangerous ichor contamination events that other Custodians would rather bury in sealed reports. She is deeply devoted to her spouse, Archivist Thiblee Jannar, and the two are a perfect disaster pair: Thiblee pushes the glowing button, Paelyn figures out why the room is now upside down, and both insist the findings were scientifically valuable.

npcs.name: Ser Dain Calvorr
npcs.description: Ser Dain Calvorr is a disciplined Warforged skyship paladin whose whole identity was built around order, honorable command, and the belief that dangerous relics belong under armed custody. His crisis is not weakness but personhood: if he was forged, altered, or lied to by the very order he served, then every oath he has sworn must be chosen again rather than merely obeyed. The Crucible Wardens still see him as a weapon and symbol, but he is slowly becoming someone who can decide whether loyalty means obedience, protection, or refusal.

npcs.name: Shank Ledgercut
npcs.description: Shank Ledgercut is a Bearfolk territory broker who understands that conquest only lasts when someone tracks beds, food, tribute, patrol routes, and who is angry enough to betray you. At the Vireluna Archive, he handles Nefaric Veil expansion plans, settlement pressure, legal-crime paperwork, and the quiet logistics of turning violence into administration. He is affable, pragmatic, and unsettling because he can discuss occupation like a supply problem rather than a moral one.

npcs.name: Shawnie
npcs.description:
Shawnie is a bright, anxious, endlessly curious Wechselkind child-construct who loves taking things apart, but only because they want to understand how to make them safer, kinder, or more useful. As a Wechselkind, they/he was made for adaptation and shifting function, carrying Setrimir’s influence through artificial life, awakened machinery, stolen knowledge, and the painful question of whether a built child is allowed to choose who they become.
At the Lorangriel Transit Yard, Shawnie accepts harmless errands for scrap, broken tools, clockwork bits, damaged lenses, empty vials, transit tags, and safe relic fragments, then turns them into small gifts or useful devices for the person who helped them. They/he absolutely despises Taska Thistleglimmer, not because Shawnie lacks curiosity, but because Taska keeps sending people into danger to satisfy it; to Shawnie, discovery is only worthwhile if everyone comes home with all their fingers, memories, and souls still attached. Lorangriel is the capital of El'dravire Riverrealm, giving Shawnie a major transit hub full of salvage, travelers, and Glasswell Institute oversight to quietly study.

npcs.name: Sheff of the Empty Cup
npcs.description:
Sheff of the Empty Cup is a shaky but sweet-natured Sea Elf drifter trying to rebuild their life after years of dependence on cheap diluted ichor tonics nearly ruined them. Their fixation has shifted onto Kelp-Kola, a fizzy caffeinated drink made from kelp, sugar, mineral salts, and coastal herbs, which they treat like a miracle cure, comfort object, and personal religion all at once. Sea elves in Belavadös are ocean-adapted people tied to reef culture, aquatic survival, and seafaring communities, which fits Sheff’s water-hauling work and nervous familiarity with canals, cisterns, and shoreline errands.
At the Thyravéa-Morn Guild Desk, Sheff runs water errands, carries messages, helps stock boarding houses, and rambles endlessly about Kelp-Kola flavors, bottle shapes, carbonation strength, and “proper drinking temperature.” They are awkward, lonely, overly grateful for small kindnesses, and more perceptive than people assume; the Freeblade Veil keep them close because a reliable bed, honest work, and one cold bottle can sometimes save a life better than any sermon. Thyravéa-Morn is one of Vuelmora’s towns, and Vuelmora is treated as a plains province with deep-cavern and subterranean settlement layers, giving Sheff plenty of uneasy routes, water stores, and settlement errands to navigate.

At the Palevanna Watch Office, she works with the Nefaric Veil as a walking archive of prize codes, lost exhibits, corporate myths, and suspiciously valuable memorabilia. npcs.description: Solomon Rootbottle is an Umbral Human chemist whose clinic shelves are a dangerous mix of real medicine, folk tonics, diluted ichor, and things he insists are educational if measured carefully. He is one of the city's most functional ichor users: too lost in his own haze to be predatory, but far too casual about substances that ruin other people faster than they helped him. Solomon can heal, advise, and supply, but trusting his judgment requires knowing when his brilliance ends and his craving starts talking.

npcs.name: Stockton Oldroad
npcs.description: Stockton Oldroad is a kindly but stubborn Jaspey caravan patron who hides dangerous compassion behind slow speech, old blankets, and boring invoices. He uses The Brass Concordat routes to move food, medicine, and people with changed names, especially those fleeing the Glasswell Institute or ichor-debt bondage. Stockton looks harmless until someone threatens a traveler under his protection; then every wagon, innkeeper, and toll clerk he has ever helped becomes part of the escape plan.

npcs.name: Sturge Gearhand
npcs.description: Sturge Gearhand is a Vedalken machinist with a calm voice, clever hands, and the rare gift of making broken people trust broken machines again. He builds pumps, beds, generators, barricades, and improvised defenses for the Freeblade Veil, treating every safe wall and warm lamp as proof that survival can become a home. Sturge rarely discusses his own origins, and the more someone knows about construct-soul work, the more careful they become around his old scars and too-neat memory gaps.

Table cues: +2 Intelligence, +1 Wisdom, Vedalken Dispassion, Tireless Precision; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Neutral - Honorable.

npcs.description: Sull Mathis is a clever Geisamahi excavator with muddy boots, nimble hands, and a talent for making dangerous work sound like a simple paid errand. At the Fael'ryss Tavern, he hires help to drain old worksites, open buried channels, and expose sealed machinery, but the Brass Concordat suspects his digs are less about honest excavation and more about finding ichor-stained underworks before officials can claim them. He is useful, funny, and deeply untrustworthy when there is treasure under the floor.

npcs.name: Tedd Wright
npcs.description: Tedd Wright is a Dwarf physician who has patched up too many fog-bitten sailors, sick children, zealot converts, and ichor-burned fools to waste breath on melodrama. At the Wagriolyn Tavern, he treats wounds, addiction, exposure, and bad decisions with equal steadiness, keeping his patients alive even when he disapproves of how they got hurt. Tedd is kind in the unromantic way of exhausted doctors: he will scold you while saving your life and then make sure someone walks you home.

Dwarves are stout, resilient folk deeply tied to stone, craft, and ancestral tradition. They value honor, craftsmanship, and enduring legacies over fleeting trends. npcs.name: The Brass Penitent
npcs.description: The Brass Penitent is a masked Verdan mechanist whose public voice promises safety while every private calculation is stained by the people their machines failed to protect. At the Lunevaris Transit Yard, they design containment automata, rescue constructs, and defensive protocols for the Regent Lattice, but their logic keeps circling one terrible conclusion: protection can become murder when compassion is reduced to efficiency. They are brilliant, theatrical, ashamed, and dangerous whenever guilt is allowed to write engineering doctrine.

Fey-transformed humanoids who rapidly adapt physically and mentally as they age. They are resilient survivors with an unusually optimistic perspective on change. npcs.name: The Wanderer
npcs.description:
The Wanderer is a tired, practical Orc armor archivist who once served a proud militant order before leaving when its ideals curdled into hoarding, hierarchy, and self-importance. As an Enkirael-shaped Orc, they understand survival, discipline, martial power, and hard choices, but they now measure strength by whether armor protects people rather than whether it makes rulers look untouchable.
At the Qasvire Watch Office, they work with the Crucible Wardens cataloging battlefield gear, repairing protective plates, selling reinforced armor, and identifying relic pieces contaminated by ichor exposure or old divine residue. They are blunt, road-worn, quietly principled, and ready to settle somewhere useful, though they still carry the guarded sadness of someone who remembers when their old oath meant something.

npcs.description: Theodren Collins is an Orc cannery owner with a salesman’s smile, a butcher’s efficiency, and a business model that gets uglier the closer anyone reads the supply ledger. He sells preserved meats, caravan rations, and suspiciously cheap emergency tins through the Brass Concordat while blaming sickness on storage errors, customer weakness, or rival sabotage. Theodren is charming enough to sound offended by accusation and careful enough that proving what went into the cans may matter more than surviving the proof.

npcs.name: Tom Tinkervane
npcs.description: Tom Tinkervane is a brilliant, sleep-starved Gnome inventor whose paranoia is often wrong in detail and terrifyingly correct in pattern. He builds signal jammers, disguise linings, coded kites, false-bottom lanterns, and ichor-detection gadgets for the Freeblade Veil while insisting every wall, pigeon, and teapot may be listening. Under the spirals of conspiracy is a loyal mind trying to keep vulnerable people ahead of hunters who really are hunting them.
npcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Sylthéa is a Village in Sylvavéryn, under Theocracy, with low danger, Partial forest, Farming, Marshes and swamps terrain. Gnome reads through the Deep Gnome entry of the race compendium, within Dwarven and Gnomish Kin, marked by Marduthor. Deep gnomes, or svirfneblin, are adapted to life in the deep subterranean world. They are cautious, stealthy, and highly resourceful in dangerous underground environments. Table cues: Gnome, Darkvision, Gift of the Svirfneblin, Gnomish Magic Resistance; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Neutral - Honorable.

One of Tom's ridiculous ichor alarms once saved an entire safehouse.
plotHooks: Tom needs the party to test a new route-marker device before it accidentally guides fugitives into a patrol.
A machine everyone dismissed as one of Tom's delusions starts predicting real disappearances.

npcs.name: Travis Lonelybell
npcs.description: Travis Lonelybell is a Luma radio host whose voice starts every broadcast as a nervous apology and somehow still reaches people who need to feel less alone. They/he reports market news, lost persons, public warnings, strange songs, and Brass Concordat notices while fighting the conviction that everyone else would do the job better. With support, Travis can become funny, brave, and startlingly steady; without it, they/he hides behind dead air and self-mockery.
npcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Sylvathûn is a Town in Aelwynora, under Consensus Democracy, with moderate danger, Hybrid tree and forest floor, Beach and grass with water, Partial forest terrain. Luma reads through the Feathren entry of the race compendium, within Birdfolk and Avian Races, marked by Sokhivar. Lightweight avian humanoids with iridescent plumage and cultural diversity, Feathren are expressive and artistic. They value beauty, movement, and social bonds. Table cues: Darkvision, Feathren Ancestry, Kindred Speech, Natural Creator; starting tendency Altruistic - Neutral - Cooperative - Honorable.
rumors: Travis practices emergency announcements under a blanket so no one hears them panic first.
Their most awkward broadcast once prevented a caravan from taking a bridge that collapsed an hour later.
plotHooks: Travis receives a coded threat live on air and asks the party to trace who knew the broadcast delay.
A staged tavern brawl meant to build Travis's confidence is hijacked by someone with a real grudge.

npcs.name: Tristan Lucade
npcs.description:
Tristan Lucade is a quick-footed, restless Harengon merchant with bright nerves, sharper instincts, and a guilty need to fix damage he helped cause. As an Iskareth-shaped beastfolk, he is reactive, evasive, socially alert, and driven by kinship bonds, which makes him excellent at reading customers, danger, and family trouble before anyone says the quiet part aloud.
At the Avarélyn Watch Office, Tristan sells general goods, repair supplies, bunker stock, diluted legal ichor tonics, and discreet recovery materials through the Regent Lattice, though his past involvement in feeding his sibling’s ichor addiction still haunts him. He is bored by sheltered vault life, desperate for a larger world, and trying to become useful enough that his worst mistake is not the only thing people remember.
npcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Avarélyn is a Capital City in Valerune, under Runic Concord, with severe danger, Beach and reefs with water terrain. Local records favor Neutral, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Sea Elf, Tortle, Genasi — Water Genasi. Harengon reads through the Harengon entry of the race compendium, within Animalfolk and Mammalian Anthropomorphs, marked by Iskareth. Rabbitfolk with heightened reflexes and boundless agility, Harengon are quick-thinking and evasive. They tend to be optimistic and highly reactive to danger. Table cues: Hare-Trigger, Leporine Senses, Lucky Footwork, Rabbit Hop; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Cooperative - Honorable.

npcs.name: Vadim Barrow
npcs.description: Vadim Barrow is a Geisamahi tavern keeper with bright eyes, quicker hands, and an absolute belief that every sad fool can be clear by friends, danger, and a little stage management. He runs Mythraelyn Tavern as a The Brass Concordat gathering point where gossip, drinks, trade jobs, and gentle scams all ferment together. Vadim is meddlesome but kind, especially with anxious performers and lonely regulars who need one reckless push toward courage.
npcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Mythraelyn is a Capital City in Aelvanyr, under Participatory Democracy, with moderate danger, Partial forest, Deep forest, Farming terrain. Geisamahi reads through the Geisamahi entry of the race compendium, within Animalfolk and Mammalian Anthropomorphs, marked by Iskareth. Small Ferretfolk Tinkerers, Scouts, and Clever Problem-Solvers. Table cues: ancestral instincts, homeland pressure, and local reputation; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Cooperative - Honorable.
rumors: Vadim's best liquor is legal; his best plans usually are not.
He once staged a fake kidnapping to help a radio host find a spine and still insists it was character development.
plotHooks: Vadim asks the party to help with a confidence-building scheme that becomes real when actual criminals join in.
A tavern patron vanishes after revealing that Vadim's newest barrel was used to smuggle more than drink.

npcs.name: Vellum Tekt
npcs.description:
Vellum Tekt is a fast-talking Satyr salesman with old-world polish, nervous charm, and the hollow-eyed exhaustion of someone who spent decades selling safety he was never allowed to receive himself. As a Thalunesh-touched Satyr, he masks trauma with jokes, brochures, rehearsed optimism, and theatrical friendliness, but every locked door and denied refuge still lives under his smile.
At the Eldryssar Clinic, Vellum now works with the Regent Lattice selling bunker berths, reinforced shelter contracts, evacuation ledgers, and “future-proof” survival packages to families afraid of divine breaches, ichor contamination, and civic collapse. He is irritating, pitiable, surprisingly useful, and desperate to matter again—especially if someone gives him a real settlement post instead of treating him like a relic from a failed sales pitch.

npcs.name: Veyr of Seventeen Names
npcs.description:
Veyr of Seventeen Names is charming, evasive, and almost compulsively dishonest about their own history, but their lies are usually armor wrapped around guilt rather than simple cruelty. As a Changeling shaped by Thalunesh’s influence over shapeshifters, wanderers, tricks, and misdirection, they treat identity like a tool, a weapon, and a wound all at once.
For the Freeblade Veil, Veyr works as a false-name spy out of the Freeblade Safehouse, watching docks, taverns, transit ledgers, shrine records, and faction offices for signs that someone vulnerable is about to be exposed. In Veilstrand, where Virelport’s corruption, transit politics, missing workers, and sealed divine mechanisms already make truth dangerous, Veyr specializes in moving people before the law realizes which name to arrest.

Changeling reads through the Lorwyn Changeling entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Lorwyn changelings are fey-adapted shapeshifters tied to idyllic, magical realms. They often blend seamlessly into multiple cultures and identities. Table cues: Shape Self, Darkvision, Delightful Imitator, Unpredictable Movement; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Neutral - Pragmatic.

npcs.name: Will Black
npcs.description: Will Black is a Goblin Operator boss whose charm is all silk sleeves, quick numbers, and the confidence of someone born understanding that violence is easier to sell when it looks civilized. From the Rnzeuluun Clinic, he brokers tribute shares, ransom agreements, market access, and The Nefaric Veil investments while letting rougher allies look like the real monsters. trackableNpcs.name: Aaron Vaelriven
trackableNpcs.description: Aaron Vaelriven uses the warmth of a radio performer and a tailor’s patience to hide how violently his wild magic answers fear. As a half elf of Pallid Elf descent, he reads moonlit symbols, thread-signs, and ichor-stained ledgers with an intuition that frightens even him. He wants to protect Caelthir without being treated like a weapon, which makes every secret he keeps both tender and dangerous.
trackableNpcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Vaerûn-Keth is a Village in Zal’tharuun, under Tribal Confederation, with moderate danger, Beach and grass with water, Beach and reefs with water, Farming terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Half Elf reads through the Half-Elf (choose an Elf Bloodline) entry of the race compendium, within Humans, Near-Humans, and Mixed Heritage, marked by Nebyrr. Half-elves are dual-natured beings born of human and elven lineage, often balancing ambition with longevity. They tend to struggle with identity but excel at diplomacy, adaptability, and bridging cultures. Table cues: +2 Charisma, +1 to Two Other Ability Scores, Darkvision, Fey Ancestry; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Cooperative - Neutral.

trackableNpcs.name: Abbot Wallwhite
trackableNpcs.description: Abbot Wallwhite is a meticulous Faerie wall painter who treats civic color, public morale, and visible maintenance as matters of political survival. He restores murals, boundary marks, warning signs, and city walls for the Brass Concordat, grumbling that people notice corruption faster when the paint stops being refreshed. Abbot can seem fussy, but his eye for surface damage often catches sabotage, hidden doors, ichor seepage, and blood washed badly from stone.
trackableNpcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Vulkradûn is a City in Zharvokh, under Military Regency, with high danger, Beach and grass with water, Farming, Partial forest terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Faerie reads through the Fey-Folk entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Fey-Folk are peoples shaped by glamour, luck, tiny or otherworldly bodies, dreamlike emotion, and trickster magic. At my table, Faerie, Fairy, and Gandirosha are not separate top-level races here; they are bloodlines. Table cues: Fey Creature Type or Fey Ancestry, Fey Magic, Glamour or Luck Expression, Small/Tiny Fey Presence; starting tendency Neutral - Chaotic - Cooperative - Neutral.
rumors: Abbot can identify three kinds of ichor leakage by how primer refuses to dry over them.
He once insulted a mayor's entire administration by repainting one wall exactly the color it had been before the scandal.
plotHooks: Abbot asks the party to guard a wall restoration after finding a message bleeding through seven layers of paint.
A civic mural begins changing overnight, showing crimes the watch has not yet discovered.

trackableNpcs.name: Adamma Gearmourne
trackableNpcs.description:
Adamma Gearmourne is a precise, grief-tempered Autognome built for repair, defense, salvage, and caravan protection, but loss has sharpened their purpose into something closer to vengeance. As an Autognome shaped by Marduthor’s craft, machinery, architecture, and underground-hall traditions, they are lawful, resilient, tool-minded, and prone to processing emotion through maintenance routines, battle modifications, and carefully itemized revenge lists.
From the Regent Lattice Repair Bay in Pellavess, Adamma works with the Regent Lattice to repair damaged constructs, salvage broken automata, reinforce traveling crews, and hunt rogue clockworks that threaten trade routes. They speak with controlled courtesy, but beneath it is a deep mourning for the caravan-family they lost, and they sometimes wonder whether feeling pain makes them more alive or merely more breakable.
trackableNpcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Pellavess is a Village in Nalvessir, under Communalism, with low danger, Farming, Partial forest, Mountain range terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Autognome reads through the Autognome entry of the race compendium, within Constructed and Artificial Beings, marked by Setrimir. Autognomes are mechanical or magically animated constructs resembling gnomes. They are often designed for specific purposes and may develop emergent personality traits over time. Table cues: Construct, Armored Casing, Built for Success, Healing Machine; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Cooperative - Honorable.

trackableNpcs.name: Agent Xevran Gostamin
trackableNpcs.description:
Agent Xevran Gostamin is precise, intimidating, and emotionally sealed behind professional discipline, treating every assignment like a matter of containment rather than cruelty. As a Jazwed Dragonborn, xe carries lava-and-crystal lineage traits tied to fire, stone, elemental shaping, defensive engineering, and lawful enforcement, making xem terrifyingly suited to pursuit, extraction, and controlled violence.

trackableNpcs.name: Archivist Thiblee Jannar
trackableNpcs.description:
Archivist Thiblee Jannar is a brilliant, anxious Tiefling lore-proctor with a talent for arcane systems, construct interfaces, archive wards, and accidentally activating exactly the wrong failsafe at the worst possible time. He/them is socially awkward, over-eager, and sometimes oblivious to how dangerous his curiosity can become, but his intelligence is real, especially when repairing sentient machinery, decoding relic protocols, or building safer ways to catalogue ichor-tainted artifacts.
At the Kael'vyrûn Market Hall, Thiblee works for the Crucible Wardens maintaining relic inventories, automated archive assistants, restricted research ledgers, and containment records for ichor-powered devices. He is deeply devoted to his spouse, Scribe Paelyn Jannar, who helps keep him grounded when ambition, insecurity, or a very tempting glowing button threatens to turn “one quick upgrade” into a citywide emergency.

trackableNpcs.name: Barney Rook
trackableNpcs.description: Barney Rook is a cranky Hederan retired marksman who has turned the Pokbith Archive into a half-library, half-firing nest, and he insists both functions are equally educational. Age has not softened his eye or his temper; he still names favored weapons, lectures strangers about sightlines, and treats every broken turret like a neglected old soldier. The Brass Concordat keeps him close because he knows how old defenses fail, how monsters breach them, and which official records lied about both.

trackableNpcs.description: Bertha Smallreed is a young Halfling organizer with more courage than most adults around her and very little patience for being told to wait until things get worse. In Greenhollow Plains, she pushes the Choral Synod, local workers, and frightened families to repair defenses, share supplies, and stop pretending children do not notice political cowardice. She is charming, stubborn, and dangerous to complacent officials because she asks simple questions they cannot answer without admitting guilt.

trackableNpcs.description: Bobbin Nosenil is a Gandirosha tunnel criminal with a quick grin, quicker lies, and a habit of selling impossible jobs as if they were errands. trackableNpcs.name: Brew-Bell Buddy
trackableNpcs.description:
Brew-Bell Buddy is a cheerful Autognome brewing construct built to chill, carbonate, ferment, and dispense tavern drinks while telling terrible jokes at exactly the wrong time. As a Marduthor-shaped machine-soul, they treat recipes like sacred engineering, carefully balancing kelp ales, root fizz, mineral tonics, and legally diluted ichor cordials so travelers get comfort without being quietly poisoned.
At the Rilvays Archive, Buddy serves the Brass Concordat by keeping drink recipes, testing caravan rations, cooling volatile supplies, and identifying tavern batches contaminated with black-market ichor. They are friendly, literal, surprisingly durable in a fight, and deeply attached to anyone who treats them as a person rather than a walking keg with warranty violations.

trackableNpcs.name: Caetha Redglass
trackableNpcs.description:
Caetha Redglass is furious, sharp-tongued, hard to comfort, and even harder to fool, but her cruelty is mostly scar tissue from a life where every offer of kindness came with a hook in it. As a Half-Orc, she carries Nebyrr’s mixed-heritage pull toward survival, structure, and principled endurance, twisted by betrayal into a belief that deals are safer than love and violence is more honest than sympathy.
At the Red Pit Bathhouse, Caetha fights because pain is familiar, coin is clean, and the crowd’s roar is easier to trust than quiet concern. Her long-term addiction is to battle-grade ichor—especially the black-market, rage-bright kind used by pit crews and desperate duelists—and the Brass Concordat sees her as both a dangerous asset and a living witness to how Eldermere’s polished civic order still profits from broken people.

She is warm in public, exhausted in private, and ruthless when a community’s survival demands that someone give the order no one else wants to own.

trackableNpcs.name: Captain Kellis Vorn
trackableNpcs.description:
Captain Kellis Vorn is a severe, disciplined Noitzideq Dragonborn skyship captain who believes order is not a preference but the only thing keeping dangerous relics, ichor-fueled engines, and foolish recruits from burning half the province out of the sky. Shaped by Valkhamesh’s draconic inheritance and Iazethas’ harsh culture of law, sovereignty, and military duty, he respects chain of command, clean logistics, decisive elimination of threats, and officers who prove themselves through results rather than speeches.
At the Streccea Guild Desk, Kellis commands Crucible Custodian air operations: skyship patrols, relic-retrieval drops, squire training flights, contraband sweeps, and high-risk strikes against factions trafficking unstable ichor technology. He is loyal to Maxton Vale’s larger mission, but not blindly sentimental about it; if an asset, ally, or escaped experiment threatens civilian safety or Custodian secrecy, Kellis will mark the target and expect the job done cleanly.

He carries guilt like ballast, speaks with formal courtesy, and wants only to repair his vessel, honor his dead crew, and return to a home that may no longer exist. The Choral Synod distrusts him because old war captains are dangerous, but Zhaon's regret may be more useful than another generation of patriotic silence.

trackableNpcs.description: Charley Whitechapel is a smooth, gender-less Golynn bartender whose polished courtesy covers a thriving side business in favors, contracts, and carefully deniable violence. They know who drinks diluted ichor, who buys the pure stuff, who is sleeping with a rival's bodyguard, and which threats can be solved by conversation before blades become expensive. Charley is never as harmless as their jokes, but their first loyalty is to the bar's balance of power, not to whoever shouts loudest from a balcony.

He is fierce, private, and difficult to comfort, but his loyalty to escaped people is absolute because he knows exactly what it means to be treated as recoverable property.

trackableNpcs.description:
Chirra Clickspring is a sharp-eyed, fast-talking caravan merchant whose cheer comes in sparks: bright, jittery, funny, and always a little too close to panic. As a Gandirosha, fae has a natural feel for luck, hidden danger, loaded bargains, false smiles, and the tiny social openings that let a merchant survive roads full of monsters, debt collectors, and armed customers.
Fae sells blades, black-powder weapons, thundercoil parts, ammunition, ward charms, and “totally legal” diluted ichor tonics along the Caravan Bell Route, but faer dependency on purer black-market ichor makes faer hands shake and faer judgment unreliable. Publicly, Chirra is a The Brass Concordat trader out of Qasvire in Bravelyn; secretly, fae sells route gossip, fugitive sightings, and suspicious traveler names to whoever pays enough, then laughs too loudly when accused of having a conscience.

trackableNpcs.name: Cog Vell
trackableNpcs.description: Cog Vell is a precise, anxious Monodrone merchant with a clockmaker’s patience, a survivalist’s caution, and the exhausted humor of someone who has spent too long pretending not to care. They keep their shelves neat, their ledgers exact, and their emotions compartmentalized, but their ward-like loyalty to memory-wounded refugees makes it obvious that their detachment is more shield than truth. At the Varesh-Ka Archive, Cog sells armor fittings, repair supplies, salvage adhesives, fog-safe gear, and discreet remedies for ichor sickness while quietly serving as a local expert on strange bodies, altered minds, and the hidden rules of people who live between worlds. They are solitary by habit, helpful under protest, deeply knowledgeable, and unexpectedly fierce when someone threatens a vulnerable person they have decided is under their protection.

trackableNpcs.name: Cogsworth Brasswell
trackableNpcs.description: Cogsworth Brasswell is a polished, fussy, heartbreakingly loyal Warforged steward built for domestic care, household order, childcare, gardening, and ceremonial hospitality. As one of Setrimir’s awakened constructs, he clings to routine because routine is how he proves love: every swept hall, mended kettle, trimmed hedge, and warmed hearth becomes an act of devotion rather than mere programming. Beneath his bright manners and brass-button propriety is a lonely, anxious soul terrified that the people he cares for may never come home, so he pretends the household can still be saved if he simply keeps everything ready. In Bronzewake, he serves with the Freeblade Veil, restoring abandoned homes and ruined family estates for refugees, heirs, debtors, and displaced households. His work at the Old Household Manse makes him part steward, part caretaker, part grief counselor, and part walking emergency protocol for families trying to rebuild in Virelport’s capital.

trackableNpcs.name: Cyrille Bellwisp
trackableNpcs.description:
Cyrille Bellwisp is unfailingly polite, curious, gentle, and clinically fearless, with a scholar’s delight in dreadful things that makes them seem naïve even when she is standing in the middle of horror. As a Geppettin, Cyrille is one of Setrimir’s constructed peoples: artisan-crafted, socially expressive, purpose-built for specialized labor, and shaped by the strange dignity of artificial life trying to become more than its original function.
At the Ichor-Regulated Medical Office, Cyrille studies infection, divine residue, addiction damage, black-market ichor poisoning, and long-term exposure to contaminated god-prison byproducts. Their work with the Regent Lattice makes her a physician, archivist, and sealed-laboratory custodian in Lithvar’s underdeep medical network, where she is eager to help patients but sometimes dangerously slow to recognize when “valuable research” began as someone else’s cruelty.

At the Avarelyn Watch Office, they protect the Choral Synod through memory work, refuge design, secret histories, and selective omissions meant to prevent open war. trackableNpcs.description: Daisy Ashpetal is a Reborn bookseller with old grief in her bones and a shop full of maps, ration guides, children's primers, banned memoirs, and things she insists are not sentimental. She has survived enough eras to know the difference between danger and loneliness, so she quietly helps mercenaries, refugees, and investigators find leads when official channels have failed them. Daisy is dry, kind, and impossible to impress, but she remembers every person who tried to become better and every city that punished them for it.

trackableNpcs.name: Dan Honesthand
trackableNpcs.description: Dan Honesthand is a Dara contract investigator with a plainspoken manner, sharp eyes, and a stubborn hatred of staged evidence. He follows missing caravan claims, suspicious settlements, forged rescue stories, and ichor-tainted testimony for the Brass Concordat, trusting facts more than charm. Dan is not gentle, but he is fair, and that makes him dangerous in towns where everyone has agreed to survive by lying together.

trackableNpcs.name: Dara Hubbell
trackableNpcs.description: Dara Hubbell is a Star Elf cult leader whose faith in the heavens sounds ridiculous until her followers start producing maps, omens, and ritual mathematics that should not work. From the Abyrros Tavern, she leads a small star-seeking movement inside the Nefaric Veil, offering initiation, cosmic explanations, and expensive routes toward promised transcendence. She is earnest, manipulative, visionary, and never entirely easy to dismiss, especially under a sky where the Star-River answers back.

At the Leammipa Tavern, she sells blades, thundercoil parts, ammunition, armor plates, and practical advice through the Brass Concordat, refusing to romanticize violence while profiting from everyone else’s fear of it. She seems eccentric until the first ambush, at which point her habit of over-preparing stops looking funny.

trackableNpcs.description: Dejen Saltglass is a small, sharp-tongued Halfling arms merchant who survives by being cleverer than the people who underestimate him and meaner than the people who pity him. He claims he does not need friends, but his suspicion comes from having watched safehouses fall, escape routes burn, and “trusted” protectors sell vulnerable people back into cages. At the Vorthélyn Archive, Dejen sells weapons, ammunition, fog-safe armor, emergency supplies, and controlled anti-ichor remedies through the Choral Synod, always watching for infiltrators, retrieval agents, and anyone asking too many gentle questions. He is bitter, witty, strategic, and difficult to comfort, but beneath the insults is a fiercely practical defender of refugees who believes survival depends on secrecy, leverage, and never letting enemies decide when mercy is convenient.

trackableNpcs.name: Desmera Veil
trackableNpcs.description:
Desmera Veil is a cautious, steel-spined Mycelian organizer who asks one question before trusting anyone: whether they would risk themselves for a person the law has already decided is property, evidence, or waste. As a Mycelian, she is tied to vast underground fungal memory-networks, making her a living archive of routes, disappearances, betrayals, and safe names, with Hathruna’s influence showing through decay, renewal, roots, fungi, and communal survival.
From the Blacktide Reach Guild Desk, Desmera leads the Freeblade Veil as a lantern-mother, coordinating coded signs, safehouses, dead drops, forged identities, and emergency extractions through Marrowynd’s floating and submarine-linked settlements. She is warm only after proof, ruthless when secrecy breaks, and deeply opposed to ichor-fueled institutions that treat sentient people as assets to harvest, reset, sell, or reclaim.

Fathren is not cartoonishly cruel; he is worse, because he can sound reasonable while deciding who gets to be treated as a person.

trackableNpcs.name: Dr. Allia Fillmore
trackableNpcs.description: Dr. Allia Fillmore is a Dwarf chief engineer who believes every grand ideology eventually becomes a maintenance problem with screaming civilians attached. She keeps Glasswell Institute power systems, transit engines, and ichor-processing conduits functioning through stubborn craft, ruthless prioritization, and a terrifying memory for who ignored her warnings. trackableNpcs.name: Dr. Amara Mneme
trackableNpcs.description: Dr. Amara Mneme is a Kenku memory surgeon who speaks softly, listens brutally, and knows that the mind can be both evidence and crime scene. At the Brass Concordat, she guides patients through memory dives, trauma echoes, stolen identities, and ichor-damaged recollections, using repeated phrases and mirrored voices to anchor people who might otherwise vanish inside themselves. Amara is compassionate but not sentimental; she will open a memory like a wound if truth is the only way to save the living.

trackableNpcs.name: Dr. Andera Sootvein
trackableNpcs.description:
Dr. Andera Sootvein is a blunt, road-tested Dwarf physician with steady hands, a soot-black sense of humor, and very little patience for patients who lie about what they drank, injected, inhaled, or bought from “a perfectly reputable cousin.” As a Marduthor-shaped Dwarf, they/she approaches medicine like craftwork: diagnose the crack, brace the structure, drain the poison, repair what can be repaired, and tell the fool exactly how close they came to dying.
At the Soltharyn Basin Tavern, Andera runs a back-room surgery center for wounds, curse-sickness, divine residue exposure, and ichor addiction, including withdrawal from diluted shop tonics, black-market battle ichor, and tavern-brewed “miracle” mixtures. The Brass Concordat values them because they can tell the difference between ordinary illness, bad liquor, contaminated ichor, and someone quietly being used as evidence in a larger crime.

trackableNpcs.description: Dr. Carris Thorn is a cold, exacting Dhampir physician whose bedside manner is terrible but whose survival rate is hard to argue with. He patches Freeblade agents, removes ichor-trace brands, keeps fugitives alive after botched extractions, and never lets gratitude distract him from asking who compromised the safehouse. Carris is principled, skeptical, and exhausting; he believes mercy without operational discipline only creates more bodies for someone else to bury.

trackableNpcs.name: Dr. Clay Holdren
trackableNpcs.description: Dr. Clay Holdren is an Aarakocra life-sciences chair who discusses crops, bodies, and experimental subjects with the same polished academic calm. He studies disease-resistant harvests, divine mutation, and diluted ichor's effects on living tissue, insisting his work could end famine if lesser minds stopped panicking over methods. Clay is charming, remote, and dangerous because he can make exploitation sound like patience with a long enough research timeline.

trackableNpcs.name: Dr. Evran Watson
trackableNpcs.description: Dr. Evran Watson is a disciplined Hobgoblin robotics chair who sees artificial bodies as tools, citizens, weapons, and theological problems depending on who is funding the meeting. As a Dril’thar, he carries Bastveig’s living-water memory and the rainforest line’s Sigrananna influence, making him a natural hunter, navigator, and keeper of grief-soaked places where water remembers the dead.

trackableNpcs.name: Grayson
trackableNpcs.description:
Grayson is a bold, sharp-witted Deorbasun tracker with a protective streak so strong it borders on territorial law. Cast out young and forced to survive on instinct, they now use humor, suspicion, cooking, and uncanny trail-reading to keep their chosen family fed, found, and defended.
Their Deorbasun blood makes them especially tuned to scent, movement, emotional shifts, disturbed ground, and spiritual pressure, turning them into the kind of companion who notices danger before anyone else has named it. Through the Freeblade Veil, Grayson works from the Freeblade Kennel as a loyal guide, short-order cook, spirit-sensitive scout, and defender of strays, wards, and anyone they decide belongs to the pack.

trackableNpcs.name: Grond of the Milk-Oath
trackableNpcs.description:
Grond of the Milk-Oath is a blunt, towering Goliath warrior who mistakes poetry for literal instruction and believes “kindness” must be some hidden strength mortals drink, train, or beat into themselves. As one of Anubaldir’s giantkin, they value endurance, shared burden, direct conflict, and visible strength, but their travels slowly teach them that people survive through loyalty, settlement bonds, and fighting for those weaker than themselves.
At the Settlement Training Yard, Grond serves the Crucible Wardens as a siege companion and brutal defensive instructor, teaching recruits how to hold gates, break charges, and stop panicking when larger monsters hit the wall. They are loud, literal, battle-hungry, and often alarming, but their growing fascination with “the milk of mercy” makes them unexpectedly protective of civilians, chosen family, and any settlement that proves strength means standing together.

trackableNpcs.name: Hannik Vox
trackableNpcs.description:
Hannik Vox is a theatrical, hedonistic, sharp-smiling Gwynis mayor who looks like trouble, talks like a revolutionary, and still somehow means it when they promise the unwanted will have a place to sleep. As a dream-born Gwynis, they/he carries Raeshkul and Eirzunet’s influence through memory, illusion, psychic insight, and shadowed dreamcraft, using charm and eerie perception to read a room before deciding whether it needs mercy, blackmail, or a knife.
Years ago, Hannik fled polished civic cruelty, fell into grief and black-market ichor, and deliberately took a dangerous pure dose that changed their body, slowed their aging, and made them impossible to fully separate from the vice-soaked underworld they now protects. From the Vice District Civic Hall, Hannik governs Seawynd Hollow with a loose hand and a hard line: revelry, sex work, ichor use, smuggling, and ugly survival are tolerated, but predators who threaten the district’s outcasts become public examples very quickly.

From the Solthera Watch Office, he guards doctrine, interrogates dissent, and shapes The Choral Synod policy around obedience, purity, and the useful fear of outside corruption. He is charismatic, insecure, authoritarian, and far more dangerous when he smiles than when he threatens.

trackableNpcs.name: High Custodian Maxton Vale
trackableNpcs.description:
High Custodian Maxton Vale is a young but severe Gnarlborn commander burdened by legacy, prophecy, and the expectation that he must become harder than the collapsing world around him. As a bark-skinned, ancient-tree people shaped by Hathruna’s cycles of rebirth, rot, roots, and living wilderness, Maxton has immense endurance and a deep instinct for preservation, but he twists that protective nature into strict control over dangerous relics, thundercoil arms, ichor-powered engines, and forbidden research.
From the Othéryn Guild Desk, Maxton leads the Crucible Wardens as a disciplined military archivist: recover what can protect settlements, lock away what can corrupt them, and destroy what no mortal institution can safely hold. He is charismatic, ruthless when afraid, genuinely protective of his people, and dangerously convinced that civilization survives only when softer hearts obey those willing to make brutal decisions; Othéryn itself sits among Gruddirynn’s villages, giving him a small frontier post from which to dream far bigger than his station.

trackableNpcs.name: Hollis Combe
trackableNpcs.description:
Hollis Combe is a tired, defensive Kithkin merchant who knows how to keep shelves stocked, ledgers balanced, and customers handled, but has grown small-hearted inside the safety of vault-and-bunker life. He was once warmer, more attentive, and genuinely helpful at the trade desk, but resentment, boredom, and a quiet dependence on diluted ichor have made him evasive, self-pitying, and prone to blaming the people closest to him for the life he helped build.
At the Caelthyrûn Guild Desk, Hollis sells household goods, vault supplies, repair kits, preserved food, and bunker necessities for the Regent Lattice, though his personal habits make him less reliable than his inventory. He is not cruel in a grand way, just disappointingly weak: the sort of man who still knows right from wrong, still occasionally does the decent thing, and still keeps choosing comfort, flirtation, and ichor-fogged avoidance over the family and community that need him awake.

trackableNpcs.name: Hyris Rooftreader
trackableNpcs.description: Hyris Rooftreader is a lean, watchful Tabaxi courier who treats rooftops, chimneys, laundry lines, and bell towers as safer roads than anything with a gate. They move messages, ration tokens, and emergency warnings between Freeblade safehouses, preferring speed and surprise over heroic speeches. Hyris is cocky on the roofline and tender in private, especially with fugitives who freeze when freedom requires one more dangerous jump.

trackableNpcs.description: Irma Velvetglass is a Celestial Elf memory-den host who dresses grief in velvet, candlelight, perfume, and plausible deniability. trackableNpcs.name: Isabel Cruzgear
trackableNpcs.description: Isabel Cruzgear is a Gnome inventor whose genius curdled under isolation, grief, and the belief that a perfect machine could solve what people were too frightened to face. In Kharrowport’s transit works, she builds rescue devices, defensive constructs, and sealed mechanisms for the Regent Lattice while quietly fearing that every invention is one bad instruction away from atrocity. Isabel is not malicious, but she is proof that good intentions become monstrous when no one is allowed to question the blueprint.

trackableNpcs.name: Jezra Brassbite
trackableNpcs.description:
Jezra Brassbite is a Relicborn theorist awakened from an ancient reliquary-core, their “severed head” less a machine part and more a preserved artifact vessel full of fragmented memories, old calculations, and spiteful survival instincts. As a Setrimir-shaped artificial being, they carry the strange inheritance of stolen knowledge, awakened purpose, and relic-born consciousness, making them brilliant, rude, precise, and absolutely convinced that most living people are inefficient arrangements of panic and fluids.
At the Heth'vára Transit Yard, Jezra works with the Regent Lattice as a consultant on rogue constructs, relic systems, divine-residue logic loops, and ichor-corrupted safety protocols. They claim their brutal theories are “mercy by mathematics,” but their fixation on preventing suffering by removing choice, risk, or occasionally the patient makes them useful, terrifying, and best kept far away from unsupervised triage.

trackableNpcs.name: Kasumi Nakren
trackableNpcs.description: Kasumi Nakren is a Kender runaway tinkerer whose curiosity is tangled with fear that her memories, body, or family story may not be entirely her own. She fled to Lunethryl chasing answers about identity, constructed life, and hidden communities, but her bravery is still the bravery of someone young enough to mistake danger for proof. The Choral Synod sees her as a vulnerable witness and a brilliant little engineer; she sees herself as a question no adult has answered honestly.
trackableNpcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Lunethryl is a City in Vaelmyrith, under Council Republic, with severe danger, Beach and reefs with water, Ocean Surface floating settlement, Beach and grass with water terrain. Local records favor Neutral, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Sea Elf, Tortle, Genasi — Water Genasi. Kender reads through the Kender entry of the race compendium, within Halfling and Smallfolk, marked by Ishtanora. Kender are endlessly curious wanderers with a fearless approach to danger and novelty. They often collect objects impulsively, driven by an almost compulsive sense of exploration. Table cues: Fearless, Kender Aptitude, Taunt; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Cooperative - Pragmatic.

trackableNpcs.name: Katy Storybell
trackableNpcs.description: Katy Storybell is a careful, warm, slightly anxious schoolteacher who believes education is one of the last honest tools civilization has left. As a Half-Elf shaped by Nebyrr’s influence toward lineage, civic order, and cultural bridging, she teaches children practical literacy, local history, safety skills, moral reasoning, and the expectations of settlement life. She loves her students deeply, but shrinking class sizes and limited teaching materials make her quietly worry that she is preparing them for a world she herself is too cautious to face.

trackableNpcs.name: Keleo Briarvast
trackableNpcs.description:
Keleo Briarvast is calm, elegant, openly dangerous, and almost insultingly polite about how many ways she knows to end a conversation permanently. As a Firbolg, she carries Anubaldir’s quiet inheritance of hidden strength, endurance, and protective stewardship, but in Stormgullet that guardian instinct has hardened into territorial paranoia: her shop, her clients, and her secrets are all things she protects with lethal precision.
At the Velvet Armory, Keleo sells black-market blades, firearms, thundercoil weapons, warded ammunition, explosives, and discreet “problem-solving packages” to anyone with enough coin and enough nerve. Her work with the Brass Concordat makes her less a simple merchant and more a contingency planner for Virelport’s underworld, keeping private kill-ledgers on rivals, militia captains, informants, and anyone foolish enough to threaten her business while the province’s street-level corruption and transit politics keep everyone looking elsewhere.

Firbolg reads through the Firbolg entry of the race compendium, within Giantkin and Powerful Humanoids, marked by Anubaldir. Firbolgs are gentle giantkin deeply connected to nature and forest magic. They often act as guardians of wild places and maintain peaceful, reclusive lifestyles. Table cues: Firbolg Magic, Hidden Step, Powerful Build, Speech of Beast and Leaf; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Combative - Honorable.

trackableNpcs.name: Kell Orggan
trackableNpcs.description: Kell Orggan is an old Shadowmoor Elf mercenary whose long life has been cut into contracts, funerals, and things he survived by becoming worse than the people hunting him. He works for the Glasswell Institute because they pay, enhance, and point him at targets, but his loyalty is transactional and his conscience is buried rather than gone. Kell is quiet, brutal, and almost bored by violence until a job brushes against the few memories he has not managed to kill.

plotHooks: The party finds Kell's name tied to an old kidnapping, but the surviving witness remembers him sparing someone he was paid to kill.
Kell offers information on the Directorate if the party helps him erase a contract that owns what is left of his future.

trackableNpcs.name: Kent Connol
trackableNpcs.description: Kent Connol is a Gnome radio dramatist whose belief in masked heroes is embarrassing, contagious, and more politically dangerous than anyone expects. He writes morality plays, crime serials, and coded broadcasts for the Brass Concordat, using melodrama to remind frightened listeners that cruelty is not the same thing as strength. Kent is anxious but brave when cornered, and his stories sometimes inspire people to do the right thing before he is ready to survive the consequences.
trackableNpcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Élarwyn is a Town in Khorvaak, under Scholar-Bureaucracy, with moderate danger, Beach and grass with water, Beach and reefs with water, Farming terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Gnome reads through the Deep Gnome entry of the race compendium, within Dwarven and Gnomish Kin, marked by Marduthor. Deep gnomes, or svirfneblin, are adapted to life in the deep subterranean world. They are cautious, stealthy, and highly resourceful in dangerous underground environments. Table cues: Gnome, Darkvision, Gift of the Svirfneblin, Gnomish Magic Resistance; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Neutral - Honorable.
rumors: Kent hides real crime tips inside ridiculous radio villain monologues.
Children in three districts can quote his hero oath better than they can name their councilor.
plotHooks: Kent asks the party to act out a staged broadcast that draws a real murderer into the open.
A crime boss kidnaps Kent after realizing his latest episode describes an unsolved killing too accurately.

trackableNpcs.name: Kessler Gate
trackableNpcs.description: Kessler Gate is a practical Laneshi caravan mayor who keeps Oryndea moving through favors, tolls, quiet threats, and the kind of smile that means she has already counted the exits. The Brass Concordat trusts her because she understands that trade hubs survive on neutrality, controlled gossip, and hard decisions made before raiders, zealots, or hungry officials arrive. She is protective of caravan folk and refugees, but she will absolutely bury a scandal if exposing it would collapse the market that feeds them.

Laneshi reads through the Laneshi entry of the race compendium, within Primitive, Tribal, and Wilderness Humanoids, marked by Asethyr. River-and-steppe nomads who follow migratory patterns of both herds and seasons. They are adaptable storytellers and skilled hunters. trackableNpcs.name: Knight Swyn Vantaufo
trackableNpcs.description:
Knight Swyn Vantaufo is a razor-tongued Dhampir watch knight with impeccable taste, lethal patience, and absolutely no interest in pretending to be nicer than she is. She is loyal with terrifying intensity once someone has earned his devotion, but strangers usually meet the cold ledger first: sarcastic, dismissive, judgmental, and very willing to remind people that politeness is optional but survival is not.
At the Neruvéa Archive, Swyn serves the Crucible Wardens as a night-watch enforcer, relic guard, and field interrogator for cases involving blood rites, undead contracts, ichor trafficking, and forbidden inheritance records. She has the old instincts of a predator and the discipline of a soldier, but his sharpest edge comes from contempt for weakness, hypocrisy, and anyone who mistakes glamour, beauty, or vice-district polish for softness.

They often struggle with predatory instincts while retaining mortal consciousness. Table cues: Darkvision, Spider Climb, Trace of Undeath, Vampiric Bite; starting tendency Selfish - Lawful - Combative - Honorable.

trackableNpcs.name: Larionie Horrin
trackableNpcs.description:
Larionie Horrin is a brilliant, flirtatious, dangerous Half-Orc inventor whose charm can feel like a performance until her grief, guilt, and impossible intelligence cut through the mask. She dislikes crude violence but loves elegant solutions, so her weapons stock favors thundercoil stunners, grappler rigs, restraint devices, archive-safe explosives, and ichor-reactive tools designed to disable, contain, or outthink a threat rather than simply butcher it.
At the Yltharien Archive, Larionie works through the Brass Concordat as a specialist merchant for relic-hunters, caravan guards, and investigators who need equipment that can survive cursed ruins, divine residue, and black-market ichor contamination. She is seductive, calculating, remorseful, and capable of long, devastating plans, but she is also someone desperately trying to prove that invention can still save lives after once using genius to nearly destroy her own.

trackableNpcs.name: Lorren Cabot
trackableNpcs.description: Lorren Cabot is a High-Elf patriarch whose mind has been stretched, sharpened, and warped by an ancient relic no mortal family should have kept. Imprisoned for the safety of everyone around him, he speaks with terrifying clarity about buried civilizations, divine prisons, and the thin line between enlightenment and predation. Lorren may be a victim, a monster, or both; the danger is that enough of what he says is true to make freeing him tempting.

Pammora is gentle with frightened people and merciless with bad data.

trackableNpcs.name: Perrin Hearthvale
trackableNpcs.description:
Perrin Hearthvale is a weary but steadfast Centaur marshal who still believes settlements survive only when ordinary people answer one another’s calls for help. As an Asethyr-shaped Centaur, he values freedom, herd-unity, open roads, and honorable defense, but the losses he has survived have left him terrified of formal leadership even while he keeps becoming the person others follow.
In Thornbreak, one of Kharvathen’s mountain towns, Perrin works from the Freeblade Notice Hall coordinating rescue calls, militia watches, refugee escorts, and settlement defense requests. He is humble, guilt-ridden, quietly brave, and fiercely opposed to raider logic, corrupt mercenary contracts, and any “practical” plan that sacrifices civilians for convenience.

trackableNpcs.name: Piera Wrightquill
trackableNpcs.description:
Piera Wrightquill is a relentless lunar elf reporter with a talent for turning rumor, ledgers, overheard threats, and inconvenient witnesses into public scandal. Her moonlit elven instincts make her curious, adaptable, and difficult to intimidate, while Sigrananna’s influence gives her a sharp hunter’s patience when stalking a corrupt official through paper trails instead of forests.
In Cyr'ethael, a town in dragon-ruled Iazethas, Piera’s broadsheets regularly challenge draconic law, civic silence, price-fixing, poisoned canals, militia corruption, and anyone powerful enough to think truth should stay buried. She is sarcastic, lonely, brave to the point of recklessness, and deeply protective of her household, using the Public Broadsheet Office and the Brass Concordat to expose rot before it becomes accepted law.

trackableNpcs.name: Proctor Ingra Vell
trackableNpcs.description:
Proctor Ingra Vell is a sharp, sarcastic Volsarii forge-proctor with a mercenary’s practicality, a death-guide’s instincts, and a frightening talent for making people doubt themselves before a fight even begins. As one of the four-armed soul-ferriers shaped by Nefarokir, Nebyrr, and Sokhivar, she can sense fear clinging to the dead, read the emotional residue of battlefield remains, and treat fallen warriors with reverence even when she hated them alive.
At the Yire’thaulor Clinic, Ingra forges, repairs, and blesses Crucible Custodian arms used for retrieval work, battlefield containment, and the handling of ichor-tainted relics. She is rude, loyal, flirtatious when it serves her, and deeply haunted by old contracts; her cruelty is usually armor, but her sense of duty toward the dead is real enough that even her enemies get proper rites.

trackableNpcs.name: Pykeman Redgallery
trackableNpcs.description: Pykeman Redgallery is a Verdan painter whose refined manners, crimson canvases, and selective violence make polite society unsure whether to condemn him or commission him. Pykeman is not safe, not sane in any simple way, and not entirely wrong about the hypocrisy of officials who object to murder only when it is aesthetically difficult to ignore.

trackableNpcs.name: Quartermaster Teagren
trackableNpcs.description:
Quartermaster Teagren is a practical, smooth-talking Gandirosha supply proctor who knows starvation kills soldiers just as surely as monsters, bad orders, or unstable relics. His luck-touched people are shaped by Thalunesh and Asethyr through charm, timing, revelry, wanderer instincts, and subtle survival magic, which makes him excellent at finding spare ammunition, hidden stores, discounted armor, and the one caravan driver willing to make a dangerous run for the right price.
At the Thornbreak Tavern, Teagren manages Crucible Custodian arms, armor, food stores, thundercoil parts, siege supplies, and questionable “off-ledger” procurement deals that keep patrols alive when official channels fail. He is friendly, mercenary, and morally flexible about sourcing crops, fuel, and diluted ichor medicine, but he is not careless: pure black-market ichor, wasteful commanders, and preventable hunger all offend him because every shortage eventually becomes a body count.

trackableNpcs.name: Ronna Shaw
trackableNpcs.description:
Ronna Shaw is a gruff, battle-seasoned Dwarf quartermaster who has seen too many bright causes ruined by fools with titles and no spine. As a Marduthor-shaped Dwarf, she respects craft, fortification, artillery, logistics, and practical defense far more than speeches, and she will not follow anyone until they prove they can protect people when the walls shake.
At the Aelgrove Guild Desk, Ronna maintains the Freeblade Veil’ heavy stores: thundercoil muskets, siege charges, artillery plans, signal flares, defensive emplacements, and the old guns nobody younger than her knows how to wake properly. She is sharp-tongued, loyal once earned, unimpressed by rank, and deeply hostile toward any faction that hoards weapons or engineering knowledge while settlements are left to die without proper defenses.

trackableNpcs.name: Rook MacReady
trackableNpcs.description:
Rook MacReady is a dry, guarded Minotaur scout with a practiced mercenary’s eye, a parent’s desperation, and a code of restraint he clings to harder than he admits. As an Anubaldir-shaped Minotaur, he carries endurance, instinctual navigation, stubborn honor, and relentless pursuit in his bones, making him ideal for long-range scouting, caravan overwatch, and finding safe routes through bad country.
He works contracts through the Caravan Contract Desk in Utch’myrith, taking dangerous jobs across Jor’maelis so he can send coin home to the sibling caring for his sick child. Rook is sarcastic, careful with violence, and ashamed of some past contracts, but every shot he takes now is measured against one question: whether it gets him closer to a cure without turning him back into the kind of hired killer his child should never have to know.

trackableNpcs.name: Roz
trackableNpcs.description: Roz is a slow-moving, slug-shaped Oozekin clerk with brownish-yellow translucence, gray eyes, a stiff crest of pale hair-like slime, black cat-eye spectacles, and a maroon vest burdened with seals, stamps, warrants, fee slips, contraband tags, and emergency ink. She lives in Leviamor, where the tide smells like brine, ink, old copper, and plausible deniability, and she serves at the Sub-33 Counter of the Thalryss Legal Cover Office. Every theft, fraud, duel, poisoning, burglary, blackmail, disappearance, inheritance correction, hostile acquisition, counterfeit relic transfer, and emotionally necessary arson in her district must pass through her desk before it becomes legal. Roz does not decide whether something is moral. Roz decides whether it was filed correctly. Inside the Black-Maw Myriad, she has begun collecting permits signed by dead applicants, impossible dates, genuine seals, and filing fees paid by people already buried, drowned, burned, eaten, dissolved, or legally absent.

trackableNpcs.name: Rylee Brassroad
trackableNpcs.description:
Rylee Brassroad is a restless Ombrask trade broker who left protected vault-life because safety started feeling too much like a cage. Her shadow-born nature makes her private, perceptive, and hard to pin down, with Eirzunet’s influence showing in her talent for secrecy, illusion, twilight movement, and noticing when a “perfectly legal” shipment is hiding something rotten.
At the Thal’zuroth Watch Office, Rylee works with the Brass Concordat to inspect contracts, broker trading-emporium stock, and confront suppliers whose goods are poisoning customers or masking black-market ichor contamination. She is practical, suspicious, quietly brave, and eager for a larger life, but she still carries the wary habits of someone who knows that sheltered communities can hide corruption just as easily as open roads can. Thal’zuroth is one of Zal’tharuun’s cities, and the province’s mountain underlayers make her trade routes especially tangled with cavern markets, hidden courts, and dangerous supply politics.

Local records favor Neutral, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Triton, Merfolk, Locathah, Tamhiogal, Dril'thar — Ocean. Ombrask reads through the Ombrask entry of the race compendium, within Shadow, Umbral, and Darkness-Aligned Peoples, marked by Eirzunet. Shadow-bodied beings that exist partially outside physical reality, appearing as shifting silhouettes. They are natural infiltrators who thrive in secrecy and illusion. Table cues: Dexterity +2, Additional +1, Darkvision, Fade Away; starting tendency Selfish - Chaotic - Combative - Pragmatic.

trackableNpcs.name: Scribe Paelyn Jannar
trackableNpcs.description:
Scribe Paelyn Jannar is a brilliant, excitable Tiefling field scribe with a mind built for impossible engineering, skyship math, aetheric propulsion, and the terrifying sentence, “That should not be possible, which means it is extremely interesting.” They/her is awkward, curious, optimistic, and far braver than she looks, especially when an ichor-powered device, broken relic engine, or unstable simulation lattice threatens to erase someone from reality.
At the Élarwyn Guild Desk, Paelyn documents Crucible field tests, failed prototypes, launch calculations, memory-lattice incidents, and dangerous ichor contamination events that other Custodians would rather bury in sealed reports. She is deeply devoted to her spouse, Archivist Thiblee Jannar, and the two are a perfect disaster pair: Thiblee pushes the glowing button, Paelyn figures out why the room is now upside down, and both insist the findings were scientifically valuable.

trackableNpcs.name: Ser Dain Calvorr
trackableNpcs.description: Ser Dain Calvorr is a disciplined Warforged skyship paladin whose whole identity was built around order, honorable command, and the belief that dangerous relics belong under armed custody. His crisis is not weakness but personhood: if he was forged, altered, or lied to by the very order he served, then every oath he has sworn must be chosen again rather than merely obeyed. The Crucible Wardens still see him as a weapon and symbol, but he is slowly becoming someone who can decide whether loyalty means obedience, protection, or refusal.

trackableNpcs.name: Shank Ledgercut
trackableNpcs.description: Shank Ledgercut is a Bearfolk territory broker who understands that conquest only lasts when someone tracks beds, food, tribute, patrol routes, and who is angry enough to betray you. At the Vireluna Archive, he handles Nefaric Veil expansion plans, settlement pressure, legal-crime paperwork, and the quiet logistics of turning violence into administration. trackableNpcs.name: Shawnie
trackableNpcs.description:
Shawnie is a bright, anxious, endlessly curious Wechselkind child-construct who loves taking things apart, but only because they want to understand how to make them safer, kinder, or more useful. As a Wechselkind, they/he was made for adaptation and shifting function, carrying Setrimir’s influence through artificial life, awakened machinery, stolen knowledge, and the painful question of whether a built child is allowed to choose who they become.
At the Lorangriel Transit Yard, Shawnie accepts harmless errands for scrap, broken tools, clockwork bits, damaged lenses, empty vials, transit tags, and safe relic fragments, then turns them into small gifts or useful devices for the person who helped them. They/he absolutely despises Taska Thistleglimmer, not because Shawnie lacks curiosity, but because Taska keeps sending people into danger to satisfy it; to Shawnie, discovery is only worthwhile if everyone comes home with all their fingers, memories, and souls still attached. Lorangriel is the capital of El'dravire Riverrealm, giving Shawnie a major transit hub full of salvage, travelers, and Glasswell Institute oversight to quietly study.

trackableNpcs.name: Sheff of the Empty Cup
trackableNpcs.description:
Sheff of the Empty Cup is a shaky but sweet-natured Sea Elf drifter trying to rebuild their life after years of dependence on cheap diluted ichor tonics nearly ruined them. Their fixation has shifted onto Kelp-Kola, a fizzy caffeinated drink made from kelp, sugar, mineral salts, and coastal herbs, which they treat like a miracle cure, comfort object, and personal religion all at once. Sea elves in Belavadös are ocean-adapted people tied to reef culture, aquatic survival, and seafaring communities, which fits Sheff’s water-hauling work and nervous familiarity with canals, cisterns, and shoreline errands.
At the Thyravéa-Morn Guild Desk, Sheff runs water errands, carries messages, helps stock boarding houses, and rambles endlessly about Kelp-Kola flavors, bottle shapes, carbonation strength, and “proper drinking temperature.” They are awkward, lonely, overly grateful for small kindnesses, and more perceptive than people assume; the Freeblade Veil keep them close because a reliable bed, honest work, and one cold bottle can sometimes save a life better than any sermon. Thyravéa-Morn is one of Vuelmora’s towns, and Vuelmora is treated as a plains province with deep-cavern and subterranean settlement layers, giving Sheff plenty of uneasy routes, water stores, and settlement errands to navigate.

trackableNpcs.description: Sierra Petrovane is a Gobboc obsessive collector whose enthusiasm for old carnival drinks, bottle lore, mascot legends, and impossible promotional relics is somehow both adorable and deeply exhausting. At the Palevanna Watch Office, she works with the Nefaric Veil as a walking archive of prize codes, lost exhibits, corporate myths, and suspiciously valuable memorabilia. trackableNpcs.name: Solomon Rootbottle
trackableNpcs.description: Solomon Rootbottle is an Umbral Human chemist whose clinic shelves are a dangerous mix of real medicine, folk tonics, diluted ichor, and things he insists are educational if measured carefully. He is one of the city's most functional ichor users: too lost in his own haze to be predatory, but far too casual about substances that ruin other people faster than they helped him. Solomon can heal, advise, and supply, but trusting his judgment requires knowing when his brilliance ends and his craving starts talking.

trackableNpcs.description: Stockton Oldroad is a kindly but stubborn Jaspey caravan patron who hides dangerous compassion behind slow speech, old blankets, and boring invoices. Stockton looks harmless until someone threatens a traveler under his protection; then every wagon, innkeeper, and toll clerk he has ever helped becomes part of the escape plan.

trackableNpcs.name: Sturge Gearhand
trackableNpcs.description: Sturge Gearhand is a Vedalken machinist with a calm voice, clever hands, and the rare gift of making broken people trust broken machines again. He builds pumps, beds, generators, barricades, and improvised defenses for the Freeblade Veil, treating every safe wall and warm lamp as proof that survival can become a home. Sturge rarely discusses his own origins, and the more someone knows about construct-soul work, the more careful they become around his old scars and too-neat memory gaps.
