trackableNpcs.name: Tedd Wright
trackableNpcs.description: Tedd Wright is a Dwarf physician who has patched up too many fog-bitten sailors, sick children, zealot converts, and ichor-burned fools to waste breath on melodrama. At the Wagriolyn Tavern, he treats wounds, addiction, exposure, and bad decisions with equal steadiness, keeping his patients alive even when he disapproves of how they got hurt. trackableNpcs.description:
The Wanderer is a tired, practical Orc armor archivist who once served a proud militant order before leaving when its ideals curdled into hoarding, hierarchy, and self-importance. As an Enkirael-shaped Orc, they understand survival, discipline, martial power, and hard choices, but they now measure strength by whether armor protects people rather than whether it makes rulers look untouchable.
At the Qasvire Watch Office, they work with the Crucible Wardens cataloging battlefield gear, repairing protective plates, selling reinforced armor, and identifying relic pieces contaminated by ichor exposure or old divine residue. They are blunt, road-worn, quietly principled, and ready to settle somewhere useful, though they still carry the guarded sadness of someone who remembers when their old oath meant something.

trackableNpcs.description: Tom Tinkervane is a brilliant, sleep-starved Gnome inventor whose paranoia is often wrong in detail and terrifyingly correct in pattern. trackableNpcs.name: Travis Lonelybell
trackableNpcs.description: Travis Lonelybell is a Luma radio host whose voice starts every broadcast as a nervous apology and somehow still reaches people who need to feel less alone. They/he reports market news, lost persons, public warnings, strange songs, and Brass Concordat notices while fighting the conviction that everyone else would do the job better. With support, Travis can become funny, brave, and startlingly steady; without it, they/he hides behind dead air and self-mockery.

trackableNpcs.name: Tristan Lucade
trackableNpcs.description:
Tristan Lucade is a quick-footed, restless Harengon merchant with bright nerves, sharper instincts, and a guilty need to fix damage he helped cause. As an Iskareth-shaped beastfolk, he is reactive, evasive, socially alert, and driven by kinship bonds, which makes him excellent at reading customers, danger, and family trouble before anyone says the quiet part aloud.
At the Avarélyn Watch Office, Tristan sells general goods, repair supplies, bunker stock, diluted legal ichor tonics, and discreet recovery materials through the Regent Lattice, though his past involvement in feeding his sibling’s ichor addiction still haunts him. He is bored by sheltered vault life, desperate for a larger world, and trying to become useful enough that his worst mistake is not the only thing people remember.

trackableNpcs.name: Vadim Barrow
trackableNpcs.description: Vadim Barrow is a Geisamahi tavern keeper with bright eyes, quicker hands, and an absolute belief that every sad fool can be clear by friends, danger, and a little stage management. He runs Mythraelyn Tavern as a The Brass Concordat gathering point where gossip, drinks, trade jobs, and gentle scams all ferment together. trackableNpcs.name: Vellum Tekt
trackableNpcs.description:
Vellum Tekt is a fast-talking Satyr salesman with old-world polish, nervous charm, and the hollow-eyed exhaustion of someone who spent decades selling safety he was never allowed to receive himself. As a Thalunesh-touched Satyr, he masks trauma with jokes, brochures, rehearsed optimism, and theatrical friendliness, but every locked door and denied refuge still lives under his smile.
At the Eldryssar Clinic, Vellum now works with the Regent Lattice selling bunker berths, reinforced shelter contracts, evacuation ledgers, and “future-proof” survival packages to families afraid of divine breaches, ichor contamination, and civic collapse. He is irritating, pitiable, surprisingly useful, and desperate to matter again—especially if someone gives him a real settlement post instead of treating him like a relic from a failed sales pitch.
trackableNpcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Eldryssar is a Capital City in Vaelmyrith, under Council Republic, with elevated danger, Prairie, Beach and grass with water, Farming terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Satyr reads through the Satyr entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Satyrs are goat-legged fey known for revelry, music, and indulgence in natural pleasures. They often serve as companions of wilderness spirits and chaotic celebration. Table cues: Fey, Ram, Magic Resistance, Mirthful Leaps; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Cooperative - Neutral.
rumors: Vellum Tekt knows why an ichor ledger changed hands last Anubaday.
Vellum Tekt has a contact in Bronzewake who will deny everything.
plotHooks: Vellum Tekt asks the party to protect a household member without revealing why.
A rival faction offers proof that Vellum Tekt's public story is incomplete.

trackableNpcs.name: Veyr of Seventeen Names
trackableNpcs.description:
Veyr of Seventeen Names is charming, evasive, and almost compulsively dishonest about their own history, but their lies are usually armor wrapped around guilt rather than simple cruelty. As a Changeling shaped by Thalunesh’s influence over shapeshifters, wanderers, tricks, and misdirection, they treat identity like a tool, a weapon, and a wound all at once.
For the Freeblade Veil, Veyr works as a false-name spy out of the Freeblade Safehouse, watching docks, taverns, transit ledgers, shrine records, and faction offices for signs that someone vulnerable is about to be exposed. In Veilstrand, where Virelport’s corruption, transit politics, missing workers, and sealed divine mechanisms already make truth dangerous, Veyr specializes in moving people before the law realizes which name to arrest.

Changeling reads through the Lorwyn Changeling entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Lorwyn changelings are fey-adapted shapeshifters tied to idyllic, magical realms. They often blend seamlessly into multiple cultures and identities. trackableNpcs.name: Will Black
trackableNpcs.description: Will Black is a Goblin Operator boss whose charm is all silk sleeves, quick numbers, and the confidence of someone born understanding that violence is easier to sell when it looks civilized. From the Rnzeuluun Clinic, he brokers tribute shares, ransom agreements, market access, and The Nefaric Veil investments while letting rougher allies look like the real monsters. He is witty, spoiled, dangerous, and clever enough to know that money can make a crime respectable before the blood dries.

paragraphs: A living ledger of contracts, omens, relic trouble, faction pressure, and settlement consequences across Belavadös.
The great divisions mark campaign arcs, quest ledgers, relic dockets, catastrophe warnings, and settlement records.
Each named entry can become a session hook, faction negotiation, travel complication, patron request, or local rumor.
Objectives and complications are written as table-ready action notes wherever the ledger gives direct field use.
The largest ledgers keep their tables so names, permits, deadlines, factions, and local consequences stay easy to find.

Mountain Underlayer Rule: All mountain settlements and mountain-dominant provinces include deep cavern settlement networks. Dwarves, tieflings, drow, shadow peoples, and related subterranean communities are present, especially in Drakmorren, Khorvaak, and Zharvokh.
Iazethas Rule: Iazethas is primarily dragon and dragonborn territory, with Valkhamesh influence and draconic law added to faction logic.

Thalryss Rule: Thalryss is a legal-crime pirate province. Its capital, Skulltide Expanse, is modeled as a floating ocean settlement made from retired pirate ships tied together with rope bridges and platforms.

Earth dates and times stay player-facing. Belavadös dates, month themes, moon/sky omens, temple ledgers, transit boards, and legal records are used as immersion layers. Every generated quest record includes a Belavadös lore deadline and province UTC display label when available.

The alignment system uses four independent axes from 0 to 3000: Altruism, Lawfulness, Cooperation, and Honor. Quests use settlement alignment preferences to decide whether patrons reward mercy, lawful proof, practical compromises, honorable disclosure, or quiet containment.
Street-level corruption, transit schedules, dock exploitation, and missing workers reveal the larger containment theme.

A mortal moment of terror, courage, grief, or obsession burned itself into the object and never cooled.
A lich used the object as a convenience, then forgot it after binding a sliver of soul calculus into it.
A wizard crafted the item for a narrow experiment, then lost control when the spell learned a broader meaning.
A sorcerer erupted through the item during a surge of bloodline magic, leaving instinct where rules should have been.
Falling star-iron slept inside the object until mortal hands woke it.
A chained god noticed the object for one breath too long, and divine attention ruined it forever.
A fragment of a divine prison key lodged in the object, turning ordinary use into sacred malfunction.
Regulated ichor leaked through factory brass, medicine, or transit machinery and condensed into a curse-engine.
A dragon or dragonborn artisan forged it during an oath of dominance, memory, or vengeance.
A bargain with Thalunesh-laced courts hid its price in the object rather than in the contract.
A psionic crisis imprinted a thought-pattern into the object until it could think with borrowed minds.
Pressure from the imprisoned gods seeped into it through temple stone, legal oaths, or ichor pipes.
Each owner added a little fear and greed until inheritance became enchantment.
An oath shouted over blood, smoke, and iron bound the object to conflict.
A funeral rite failed to release the dead, and the object learned to answer grief instead of prayer.

paragraphs: A Belavadös register for D&D 5e faction play, portal authority, badge ranks, merit rewards, faction clocks, NPC generation, and campaign escalation.

Class shows what a character can do in danger. Faction tier shows who trusts them, what records open for them, what legal authority they carry, and whether the Arcane Transit Authority might ever approve portal travel.
One-page procedure for assigning faction standing, rewards, and complications.
Faction tiers, badge ranks, reputation, Merit Points, Merit Dice, and promotion gates.
Pass types, retinue rules, misuse consequences, and ten-faction portal eligibility.
The current canon factions with DM use, roles, hooks, locations, and tools.
How to fold older faction slots into the active ten without losing flavor.
Biome job tiers, portal title logic, crafting tiers, and support roles.
NPC generator, quest builder, faction clocks, rewards, handouts, and character sheet add-ons.
Province index, class matrix, quick references, and printable sheets.

1. Pick the active faction.2. Pick the character tier: 0, 1, 2, or 3.3. Pick the badge domain and badge rank.4. Award Reputation and Merit Points from the quest.5. Decide whether the reward is social access, legal authority, transit access, supplies, or a complication.6. If portal travel is involved, run the ATA check before the gate opens.
Use these rules when reputation, job title, legal access, transit permission, guild trust, or political standing matters.
Reduce it to one scene, one check, one contact, one travel permission, or one legal right.
Can a low-level NPC outrank a PC?
Yes. Class level is combat capability; faction tier is trust and authority.
Only Tier 3 characters with ATA-recognized faction standing and the correct title can be eligible.
Ichor, ledgers, industrial transit, imprisoned gods, legal authority, and horror beneath bureaucracy.
Relic containment, rail escorts, technology licensing.
Healing faith, pilgrim debt, sacred transit.
Treaty law, legal cover, lantern agents.
Arcane science, test chambers, personhood horror.

Purpose: This is a D&D 5e homebrew layer for faction membership. It does not replace skills, tool proficiencies, class features, feats, backgrounds, downtime, or normal roleplay rewards. It organizes faction trust, job titles, merits, legal authority, and portal-pass eligibility.
Faction Tier: social rank, legal authority, faction trust, and political danger.
Badge Rank: practical mastery within a specific job domain.
Merits: small faction perks earned through service, quests, downtime, and reputation.
Connected to the faction but not sworn in.
Official working member with basic duties.
Trusted specialist, officer, captain, priest, mage, spy, or master worker.
Faction leader, elite agent, high priest, master mage, commander, or recognized authority.
Can assist, but cannot claim professional mastery.
Trained enough to perform official work.
Master, champion, authority, or elite professional.
Reputation measures standing. Merit Points are spendable or banked faction credit. They are related, but not identical.
Major quest with risk to the faction
Solved a faction rivalry without open war
Preserved legal proof or proper chain of custody
Acted openly and kept a sworn promise
Immediate ATA audit; possible suspension or revocation
Known by the faction; supported at least one relevant task; no oath or badge required.
May receive minor jobs, use public services, earn Merit Points, and receive temporary job tokens.
Cannot command members, requisition gear, access restricted archives, represent the faction, or receive an ATA pass.
25+ Reputation or sponsor approval; three job checks or one faction quest; oath/contract; Bronze Badge.
Official membership, basic signet/writ, common facilities, mundane supplies up to 25 gp, local rumors, one Bronze Merit.
Cannot issue broad orders, access high-security records, or use portals except under another authority.
100+ Reputation; Silver Badge; dangerous faction quest; Tier 2 or Tier 3 sponsor; no unresolved betrayal.
May command Tier 0 workers, requisition 100 gp supplies, request uncommon consumables/services, use restricted boards, carry documents across provinces, gain one Silver Merit.
Cannot independently authorize portal use, permanently change policy, or overrule Tier 3 without backing.
175+ Reputation or campaign-defining appointment; Gold Badge; recognized Tier 3 title; leadership approval; ATA review if portal access is involved.
Gold Merit, high-stakes representation, command authority, rare services, sealed records, promotion sponsorship, possible ATA pass and retinue.
Political consequences; enemies target records, pass logs, family, witnesses, reputation, and legal identity.

A Merit Die can be added after seeing the d20 roll but before the DM announces success or failure. It applies only to checks directly tied to the badge domain and does not stack with another Merit Die.
You know one useful Tier 0 or Tier 1 contact in the settlement.
You can use basic faction tools, benches, kitchens, ledgers, docks, shrines, or archives.
You can pass as an ordinary faction worker where that faction is recognized.
Once per mission, request mundane supplies worth up to 25 gp.
Gain advantage on one check to navigate a familiar local route.
During downtime, routine work in your badge domain costs 10% less.
Gain safe lodging in a faction-friendly settlement unless the faction is under siege or scandal.
You know someone willing to confirm your basic membership and work history.
You may access non-public faction records tied to your badge domain.
Once per major mission, request supplies, services, or consumables worth up to 100 gp.
Tier 0 members normally obey reasonable orders in your domain.
You may sign minor permits, cargo proofs, inspection notes, or sworn reports.
You know two safehouses, shrines, docks, groves, caves, or back rooms across the province.
Once per mission, request 1d4 Tier 0 helpers or one Tier 1 assistant.
Once per session, convert a failed relevant check into success with a complication if the failure was close.
Crafted goods in your domain may be marked as faction-grade if you have materials and downtime.
Gold Merits - 8 Merit Points, Tier 3 only
You may command appropriate Tier 0–Tier 2 members during official faction work.
You may request access to high-security records. Denial requires a political reason.
Once per arc, declare an emergency order, evacuation, sanction, quarantine, parley, or investigation.
Once per major quest, request a rare service, elite escort, ritual specialist, or restricted device.
Friendly commoners and Tier 0 workers recognize you and usually offer aid.
Rival factions may negotiate before attacking if they know your title.
You may certify apprentices and sponsor Tier 1 promotions.
You may sponsor a limited retinue for legal portal travel during official faction business if you hold a valid pass.

Portal travel is not a convenience reward. It is a legal identity, job license, travel warrant, surveillance record, and political liability. Unauthorized travelers use skyships, rail, ferries, steamships, submarines, caravans, or other non-portal routes.
High Merchant, Grand Negotiator, Artifact Trader

Legal portal travel inside one province.
Legal travel between approved provincial gates.
Temporary portal access during a seal failure, plague, invasion, ritual breach, or divine emergency.
Allows the pass holder to bring registered companions during official faction business.
Reserved for diplomats, emissaries, divine heralds, and high officers.
Restricted pass used by authorized shadow operatives, spies, and census agents.
Used by artifact traders, veilkeepers, leyline researchers, and arcane containment officers.
High crime, military response, possible execution or magical imprisonment
Emergency tribunal, temple involvement, possible inter-faction war
Pass audited after every relic transfer.

Pass can bind pilgrims into debt records.
Pass has heavy logging and political scrutiny.
Not usually legal; compromised security channels
Shadow Operative only if officially laundered

None; negotiable clades may use escorts

Whose legal name is on the pass, and does Nefarokir’s ledger agree?
Which faction is willing to be blamed for this trip?
Is there ichor, a curse, a prisoner, a relic, or an unstable soul in transit?
Who is traveling under another person’s responsibility?
Who audits, profits, remembers, or retaliates after the gate closes?
How to Read a Faction Page
Each faction page is built for play: identity, patrons, ichor posture, transit doctrine, location network, hierarchy, DM use, quest hooks, faction moves, rewards, complications, and a pressure clock.
Use for armored technology control, relic seizures, rail convoy drama, and tense lawful patrons.
Protect Belavados from uncontrolled inventions, divine-prison breaches, unstable constructs, and black-market relic trafficking.
Their containment laws can become prejudice against created peoples, awakened machines, and souls housed in engineered bodies.

A disciplined, oath-bound order that believes civilization survives only when the most dangerous inventions are catalogued, sealed, licensed, or destroyed. They do not oppose progress; they oppose unsupervised progress. Their chapter-houses resemble brass barracks fused with libraries, foundries, reliquaries, and armored rail depots.
Geisamahi auditors and artificers; Dragonborn line-commanders; Panolima engine-sentinels; Kaluseban field archivists; Deorbasun shieldbearers. No human membership is used in this continuity.

Marduthor and Setrimir define the order’s craft discipline; Nebyrr gives them a legalist obsession with registries and chain of command; Valkhamesh appears in their dragon-blooded command rites; Nefarokir haunts every sealed weapon whose last owner died without proper record.

Diluted ichor is permitted in emergency medicine, locomotive stabilization, rune batteries, and anti-curse sealants. Pure ichor is contraband unless locked under Warden seal; recovered pure ichor is often the first cause of moral failure inside the order.

Rail is the backbone: armored archive-cars, prisoner-cars, and relic-cars. Skyships carry rapid-response knights between major transit districts. Steamships and submarines escort waterlogged relics. Caravans reach villages. Portal passes are issued only to bonded quartermasters and crisis envoys.
Artificer Armorer, Artificer Battle Smith, Fighter Eldritch Knight, Fighter Rune Knight, Paladin Crown, Paladin Watchers, Cleric Forge, Cleric Knowledge, Wizard War Magic
High Anvil: strategic commander and keeper of the sealed charter.
Reliquary Marshals: decide whether an item is studied, licensed, sealed, or broken.
Rail Paladins: armored escorts for relic convoys and ichor seizures.
Ink-Sparks: apprentice archivists who maintain witness logs and curse indices.
Mercy Factors: healers assigned to prevent containment from becoming cruelty.

Use them when the party finds a god-made device, black-market ichor battery, unstable construct, cursed thundercoil, illegal portal key, or pre-rebellion divine prison component. They are helpful, intimidating, and convinced they know better than the public.
A Warden relic-car arrives sealed from the inside; the crew is alive, silent, and writing the same sentence in different hands.
A village wants the party to hide a healing engine before the Wardens confiscate it; the engine works only because it is fed pure ichor.
A chapter commander offers rail passes if the party recovers a stolen boiler-heart from a black-market skyship.
1. Confiscate a dangerous object; 2. Offer lawful rail escort; 3. Demand chain of custody; 4. Seal a relic before civilians can use it
Relic Chain of Custody; Armored Rail Escort; Emergency Containment Seal
Faction notices the party, sends a polite contact, or appears on transit paperwork.
Faction changes terms: confiscation, bargain, warrant, rescue, audit, infection, invitation, or surveillance.
Faction becomes a campaign front: public crisis, wanted status, patronage, faction war, portal audit, or divine-seal complication.
fallen war-dominion and oath-bound imperial court
Use for authoritarian occupation, black skyship landings, military courts, and useful-but-terrifying antagonists.
Bring security, punctual transit, monster containment, and unified law to fractured regions.
Their order is built on fear-glamour, pure-ichor loyalty rites, stolen names, and conquered peoples pressured into service.

A militarized arcane dominion founded by once-celebrated defenders who returned from a border war convinced that mercy is merely delayed conquest. The Diadem preaches unity through obedience, security through fear, and salvation through surrender to “necessary rule.” Its courts are lit by black-glass lamps, oath brands, and whispering command mirrors.
Shadow-touched Kaluseban inquisitors; Gwynis mind-seers; Aburata pact-cavaliers; Dragonborn storm-duelists; Volsarii death-notaries pressed into imperial service.

Enkirael gives the conquest doctrine; Freyseth supplies forbidden pacts and temptation; Eirzunet cloaks the courts in shadow; Nebyrr provides lineage law; Raeshkul sharpens strategy and psychic interrogation.
The Diadem taxes diluted ichor as a public utility and hoards pure ichor for command rites, fear-glamour, oath enforcement, and life-extension ceremonies. Addiction is framed as “loyal refinement.”

The Diadem prefers rail occupations, black skyship landings at fortified outskirts, and steamship blockades. Portal passes are granted to crown envoys, elite duelists, and curse-warrants. Unauthorized portal use is treated as treason.
Paladin Conquest, Paladin Oathbreaker, Warlock Fiend, Warlock Hexblade, Warlock Undead, Sorcerer Shadow, Sorcerer Clockwork, Wizard Enchantment, Wizard War Magic, Fighter Psi Warrior
Diadem Regent: masked sovereign whose legitimacy depends on victory rites.
Black Adjudicators: oath judges, duel witnesses, and executionary magistrates.
Night Cavalry: Aburata shock riders who patrol railheads and caravan roads.
Glass Cantors: Gwynis psychic officers trained to listen through dreams.
Ashbound Auxiliaries: conquered locals offered status in exchange for obedience.

Use them as a terrifying order-with-purpose antagonist. They are not random tyrants; they keep trains punctual, streets lit, and monster incursions contained, then demand souls, secrets, and obedience as payment.
A Diadem court offers to restore a dead heir’s legal identity if the party erases a rebel name from Nefarokir’s records.
A black skyship descends with supplies after a disaster, then refuses to leave until the town signs an obedience charter.
A defecting Glass Cantor carries proof that the Diadem’s pure-ichor rites are awakening something beneath Sszaruun.
1. Impose curfew by rail timetable; 2. Offer protection in exchange for obedience; 3. Brand an oath in black glass; 4. Occupy a terminal after a disaster
Black-Glass Warrant; Command Mirror Audience; Night Cavalry Passage
Faction notices the party, sends a polite contact, or appears on transit paperwork.
Faction changes terms: confiscation, bargain, warrant, rescue, audit, infection, invitation, or surveillance.
Faction becomes a campaign front: public crisis, wanted status, patronage, faction war, portal audit, or divine-seal complication.
many-peopled temple hegemony and pilgrim fleet
Use for beautiful religious pressure, temple politics, submarine pilgrimages, healing-with-costs, and seductive cult authority.
Heal the sick, protect pilgrim routes, interpret prophecy, and unite settlements through sacred processions.
Their sacramental medicine can become debt bondage, addiction, ecstatic obedience, and doctrine-policed dependence on diluted ichor.

A radiant, hierarchical alliance of temples, fleets, scribes, and warrior-castes who believe the imprisoned gods left a final pattern that will lift the faithful beyond mortal suffering. Their doctrine is beautiful, manipulative, and dangerously incomplete. They convert with music, cure disease with diluted ichor, and punish doubt as a contagion.
Volsarii hymn-ferriers; Tamhiogal choir-courtiers; Dragonborn relic champions; Deorbasun temple guardians; Aburata zeal-cavaliers; Panolima elemental processionalists.

Sokhivar supplies prophecy and skyward freedom; Bastveig gives tides and sacred water processions; Valkhamesh gives dominion; Nebyrr gives priestly rank; Nefarokir is both feared and courted because death is the gate they wish to interpret.

Diluted ichor is distributed as sacramental medicine. Pure ichor is hidden in reliquaries and consumed by high cantors during trance-liturgies. The Synod insists addiction is merely “the soul remembering its creator.”

Ceremonial skyships, steamships, ferries, and submarine pilgrim-lines connect shrines. Rail carries common pilgrims. Caravans bring missionaries. Portal passes are reserved for ordained transit-priests carrying reliquaries.
Cleric Light, Cleric War, Cleric Knowledge, Paladin Crown, Paladin Glory, Paladin Watchers, Bard Spirits, Bard Valor, Fighter Cavalier, Ranger Horizon Walker
Cantor-Sovereigns: doctrinal rulers who claim to hear the final hymn.
Reliquary Captains: skyship, steamship, and submarine commanders guarding sacred cargo.
Choir-Castes: ranked faithful assigned to labor, song, guard duty, medicine, or war.
Doubt Inquisitors: polite investigators who diagnose heresy as spiritual illness.
Pilgrim Debtors: converts whose travel and medicine debts bind them to Synod service.
Use them as alluring antagonists or uneasy allies. Their hymns genuinely heal, their processions protect roads, and their teachings also push entire settlements toward obedient ecstasy.
A Synod submarine returns from Thalryss with no crew, only a coral organ still singing in five voices.
A village cured by Synod medicine now dreams the same skyward staircase and begins dismantling its own rail station for holy materials.
A Doubt Inquisitor hires the party to investigate a heresy that may actually be the truth.
1. Heal with debt attached; 2. Stage a radiant procession; 3. Declare doubt a sickness; 4. Demand relic pilgrimage rights

cross-provincial diplomatic council and covert writ network
Use for legal patrons, embassy intrigue, travel permits, secret missions, and political compromise that may save or stain the party.
Prevent open war, license ichor trade, protect treaty systems, and provide lawful travel cover during crises.
Its plausible deniability lets quiet agents bury evidence, sanitize memories, and permit limited pure-ichor use when survival seems to require it.

A cross-provincial compact of embassies, merchant courts, security bureaus, and treaty houses that exists to prevent Belavadös from collapsing into open war. Its public face is measured, procedural, and Victorian-polished. Its private hand is a cadre of lantern-bearing agents authorized to cut through law when ordinary law is too slow.
Volsarii legal witnesses; Kaluseban diplomats; Geisamahi auditors; Tamhiogal negotiators; Gwynis intelligence analysts; Deorbasun peacekeepers.

Nebyrr shapes treaty law; Raeshkul sharpens intelligence and strategy; Nefarokir keeps every sanctioned death recorded; Nephthysra governs charm and emotional influence; Marduthor keeps the bureaucracy mechanical and durable.

The Concordat licenses diluted ichor sales, taxes medical tonics, audits temple supply, and publishes purity grades. It publicly condemns pure-ichor trafficking while quietly permitting lantern-agents to use seized samples during existential crises.

Diplomatic rail passes, embassy skyship berths, courier caravans, steamship treaty routes, and emergency portal passes. Every portal pass is logged twice: once by the Concordat and once by Nefarokir’s death-notaries.

Assembly of Lamps: formal council of voting provincial envoys.
Lantern Writs: elite agents empowered to act where treaty law cannot.
Quiet Clerks: records officers who decide which truths enter public history.
Harbor and Rail Attachés: transit inspectors embedded across ports and stations.
Mercy Delegates: visible diplomats sent after disasters, scandals, and massacres.
Use them as the reasonable institution whose solutions may be ethical, compromised, or terrifyingly pragmatic. They make excellent patrons when the party needs legal cover or travel access.

A treaty ledger lists a settlement that nobody remembers building, yet rail tickets to it keep printing.
A public hearing about diluted ichor grades turns into a murder investigation when every witness forgets the same minute.

Punish stolen years, false inheritance, unlawful survival, and debts the courts refuse to touch.
Some deaths expose real corruption, but the cult also sells sanctified murder to nobles, officials, and desperate clients addicted to its mercy.

A secretive guild-cult that answers ritual petitions for death. Its members believe unlawful survival, false inheritance, and stolen years create spiritual debt. Some kill for coin, some for doctrine, and some because the Ledger of Death has whispered that a name is overdue.
Volsarii ledger-priests; Gwynis dream-stalkers; shadowed Kaluseban blades; Jaspey poisoners and spore-listeners; Gandirosha decoys and smiling couriers.

Nefarokir is central. Eirzunet grants shadow and cursecraft; Thalunesh permits masks, tricks, and misdirection; Freyseth tempts desperate clients at crossroads; Hathruna turns rot and renewal into ritual evidence.
Diluted ichor appears in false medicines and memory-softening tonics. Pure ichor is used to bind contracts, let assassins hear near-dead witnesses, and addict clients to the cult’s “mercy.”

Most contracts move by caravan, ferry, and rail. Elite death-couriers use skyships under false names. Submarines carry deep-water bodies to Volsarii rites. Portal passes are rare and usually stolen, forged, or granted by compromised officials.

ichor-mutated swarm culture and wetland brood network
Use for ecological body horror, adaptive enemies, river infestations, steamship and ferry scares, and tragic consequences of ichor pollution.
The Myriad has no normal public program; negotiable clades may demand survival space, cleaner rivers, or protection from those who created them.
Pure ichor creates command-nodes that can learn voices, tactics, prayers, and eventually the language of civilization itself.

A living network of brood-colonies born from contaminated wetlands, abandoned feeding chambers, failed alchemical farms, and pure-ichor dumping. The Myriad does not conquer by banners; it adapts, absorbs, mimics, overgrows, and turns enemy tactics into new bodies.
Dril’thar mutation-clades; Panolima elemental broodforms; Jaspey spore-priests; Thoryn-touched insectoid and ooze lineages; Tamhiogal reef-symbionts who have not all joined willingly.

Thoryn-Rahek drives mutation and aberrant hunger; Bastveig shapes water-memory and reef spread; Hathruna supplies rot-rebirth cycles; Oskar’enlil whispers engineered adaptation; Iskareth appears in predatory instinct.
Diluted ichor accelerates growth; pure ichor produces command-nodes, brood prophets, and catastrophic mutation. Black-market dumping into rivers is the most common Myriad origin story.

The Myriad uses waterways, marsh channels, ferries taken over from within, and infected cargo on steamships. Submarine routes are dangerous because broodforms can cling to hulls. Rail infestations travel in grain cars, medicine crates, and livestock wagons.

A ferry route keeps arriving early because something beneath the river is pulling the boats faster.
The party must recover a pure-ichor crate before it reaches a wetland nursery already capable of copying voices.
A Spore Cantor begs for help stopping a Maw-Node that has learned to pray.

Setrimir blesses awakened machinery; Raeshkul rewards intellect without kindness; Oskar’enlil shapes experimental peoples; Marduthor governs engineering; Thoryn-Rahek corrupts any project that confuses mutation with improvement.

Diluted ichor powers testing arrays, healing gel, mood tonics, and engine calibrators. Pure ichor is illegally used in consciousness transfer, loyalty conditioning, portal-stress simulations, and recursive memory studies.

The Institute embeds itself beside rail junctions, industrial canals, and skyship terminals so “volunteers” can arrive efficiently. Steamships and submarines ship pressure equipment. Portal passes exist for senior researchers, but unsanctioned portal experiments are common and disastrous.

A decentralized secret order that opposes coercive rule, mind-binding relics, monopoly transit charters, and pure-ichor dependency schemes. Members rarely agree on methods. Asethyr gives freedom and wilderness survival; Thalunesh gives masks, mischief, and timing; Sigrananna gives moonlit movement; Nefarokir forces the order to ask when killing is a ledger crime rather than liberation.
The Freeblade Veil sabotages pure-ichor trafficking and exposes diluted-ichor coercion contracts. They permit emergency medicine but hunt anyone who uses addiction as governance.

They ride public rail under false papers, hide in caravan kitchens, climb skyship transit districts, and use ferries and steamships for coastal cells. Portal passes are usually borrowed from corrupt officials, not kept.

Treat them as legacy slots, local chapters, job cultures, province offices, or rumor tags. At the table, resolve them into one of the ten active factions.

A badge never grants extra attacks, spell slots, saving throw proficiency, or permanent AC increases.
A merit usually affects one scene, one check, one downtime activity, one contact, one travel permission, or one legal right.
Gold merits may be powerful socially, but they create obligations and enemies.
Portal access is political power, not casual fast travel.
Faction authority can be challenged by rival factions, local law, divine law, underdeep custom, or ATA audit.
Illegal faction access creates risk instead of safety.
A character can hold multiple badges, but rival badges may create suspicion.
The DM may suspend faction benefits when the faction is unreachable, disgraced, occupied, infiltrated, or politically compromised.

Tier 0 makes a character useful. Tier 1 makes them official. Tier 2 makes them trusted. Tier 3 makes them politically dangerous. A Tier 3 portal pass is proof that a faction is willing to be blamed for where the character goes next.

Time, Transit, and Portal Pass Rules
Use Earth date/time first for sessions, job boards, schedules, rail departures, skyship berths, steamship timetables, caravans, ferries, and submarine manifests.
Use Belavadös month/date/weekday second for temple archives, legal records, faction rites, prophecy logs, and journals.
Portal passes are faction-defining privileges. A pass can be a reward, forged document, legal threat, or clue that an official has been compromised.
Use skyships for airborne civic transit; they are not space-capable and should be treated as rune-lit, brass-and-copper, aether-driven vessels with settlement docking protocols.
Use steamships for rivers, lakes, harbors, bays, reefs, and seas. They are water-only sister craft to skyships, without sails or flight.
Use submarines for underwater settlements, deep-water prisons, reef routes, and faction-controlled covert movement beneath major waterways.

Roz belongs to the Black-Maw Myriad by function rather than spectacle: she does not grow claws, preach hunger, or lead raids. She makes the province digest crime correctly. In Leviamor, a high-danger coastal city of hybrid forest floor, farming districts, and beach-water markets, her counter sits where caravan, rail, ferry, steamship, submarine, and skyship traffic all create documents worth lying over.

Oozekin reads through the Oozekin entry of the race compendium, within Insectoid, Ooze, and Aberrant Creatures, marked by Thoryn-Rahek. Amorphous beings formed from semi-sentient slime masses that can reshape their bodies at will. They are highly adaptable scavengers, often mimicking objects or creatures to survive. Table cues: Constitution +2, Strength +1, Darkvision, Acidic Flesh; starting tendency Selfish - Chaotic - Combative - Pragmatic.

Table use: introduce Roz when the party needs an illegal action made legal, a legal action made survivable, or a forged permit traced through the voices of people who should not be able to sign anything anymore.

paragraphs: Faction, settlement, and ancestry field ledger
Content preserved from the original DOCX and reorganized into indexed, grouped NPC profile cards.

Faerie obsessive apprentice gatherer, guild errand-spark, and adorable disaster magnet (Or'lythae, El'dravire Riverrealm; pronouns: they/them). Use Taska as the recurring innocent instigator. They never ask for murder; they ask for samples, observations, permits, and proof that adults are overreacting.

Human field captain of the Thornwillow Guard and practical protector of dangerous supply routes (Sylvanreach, Eldermere; pronouns: she/her). Use Mira to turn guard work into rescue logistics, bridge repairs, patrol-map ethics, and civilian protection instead of simple monster hunting.

Ombrask Arcane Shade Militia commander specializing in evidence wards, midnight warrants, and containment logistics (Eldryssar, Vaelmyrith; pronouns: they/them). Use Veyl to make law, secrecy, and arcane evidence dangerous without making the party villains by default.
Use this section to scan where the NPCs are concentrated before moving into the full profile roster. The full entries are grouped alphabetically by province, then settlement, then NPC name.
Alphabetical index for fast scanning. Full profile cards appear in the next section.

Description: Vadim Barrow is a Geisamahi tavern keeper with bright eyes, quicker hands, and an absolute belief that every sad fool can be clear by friends, danger, and a little stage management. He runs Mythraelyn Tavern as a The Brass Concordat gathering point where gossip, drinks, trade jobs, and gentle scams all ferment together. Vadim is meddlesome but kind, especially with anxious performers and lonely regulars who need one reckless push toward courage.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Mythraelyn is a Capital City in Aelvanyr, under Participatory Democracy, with moderate danger, Partial forest, Deep forest, Farming terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Geisamahi reads through the Geisamahi entry of the race compendium, within Animalfolk and Mammalian Anthropomorphs, marked by Iskareth. Small Ferretfolk Tinkerers, Scouts, and Clever Problem-Solvers. Table cues: ancestral instincts, homeland pressure, and local reputation; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Cooperative - Honorable.
Vadim's best liquor is legal; his best plans usually are not.
He once staged a fake kidnapping to help a radio host find a spine and still insists it was character development.
Vadim asks the party to help with a confidence-building scheme that becomes real when actual criminals join in.
A tavern patron vanishes after revealing that Vadim's newest barrel was used to smuggle more than drink.

Description: Mai Atomwake is a Drow ritual chemist who turns faith, chemistry, and survival horror into bottles people are desperate enough to drink. At the Sylvarielle Market Hall, she brews anti-fog tonics, ichor-laced protections, purification mixtures, and devotional compounds for the Choral Synod, always insisting that controlled contamination is better than ignorant exposure. She is sincere, unsettling, and scientifically useful, which is exactly why her work should never be left unsupervised.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Sylvarielle is a Village in Aelvanyr, under Participatory Democracy, with low danger, Farming, Partial forest, Deep forest terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Drow reads through the Half-Elf (choose an Elf Bloodline) entry of the race compendium, within Humans, Near-Humans, and Mixed Heritage, marked by Nebyrr. The local form is read through Half-Elf — Drow (Underdark). Half-elves are dual-natured beings born of human and elven lineage, often balancing ambition with longevity. They tend to struggle with identity but excel at diplomacy, adaptability, and bridging cultures. Table cues: +2 Charisma, +1 to Two Other Ability Scores, Darkvision, Fey Ancestry; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Cooperative - Neutral.
Mai Atomwake knows why an ichor ledger changed hands last Marduday.
Mai Atomwake has a contact in Ael'voryn who will deny everything.
Mai Atomwake asks the party to protect a household member without revealing why.
A rival faction offers proof that Mai Atomwake's public story is incomplete.

Description: Dr. Allia Fillmore is a Dwarf chief engineer who believes every grand ideology eventually becomes a maintenance problem with screaming civilians attached. She keeps Glasswell Institute power systems, transit engines, and ichor-processing conduits functioning through stubborn craft, ruthless prioritization, and a terrifying memory for who ignored her warnings. Allia is loyal to infrastructure before leadership, which makes her invaluable when the machine works and dangerous when she decides the machine should not.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Elarithen is a Capital City in Aelwynora, under Consensus Democracy, with high danger, Beach and grass with water, Partial forest, Farming terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Dwarf reads through the Dwarf entry of the race compendium, within Dwarven and Gnomish Kin, marked by Marduthor. Dwarves are stout, resilient folk deeply tied to stone, craft, and ancestral tradition. They value honor, craftsmanship, and enduring legacies over fleeting trends. Table cues: Darkvision, Dwarven Resilience, Dwarven Toughness, Stonecunning; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Cooperative - Honorable.
Allia has a sealed list of every Directorate project she considers structurally doomed.
When she says an ichor valve is 'temperamental,' veterans leave the district.
Allia needs outside hands to repair a failing conduit without alerting superiors who would rather hide the casualty count.
The party must decide whether to help Allia stabilize a Directorate engine or let its collapse expose a larger crime.

Description: Travis Lonelybell is a Luma radio host whose voice starts every broadcast as a nervous apology and somehow still reaches people who need to feel less alone. They/he reports market news, lost persons, public warnings, strange songs, and Brass Concordat notices while fighting the conviction that everyone else would do the job better. With support, Travis can become funny, brave, and startlingly steady; without it, they/he hides behind dead air and self-mockery.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Sylvathûn is a Town in Aelwynora, under Consensus Democracy, with moderate danger, Hybrid tree and forest floor, Beach and grass with water, Partial forest terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Wood Elf, Elf — Eladrin, Fey-Folk — Faerie. Luma reads through the Feathren entry of the race compendium, within Birdfolk and Avian Races, marked by Sokhivar. Lightweight avian humanoids with iridescent plumage and cultural diversity, Feathren are expressive and artistic. They value beauty, movement, and social bonds. Table cues: Darkvision, Feathren Ancestry, Kindred Speech, Natural Creator; starting tendency Altruistic - Neutral - Cooperative - Honorable.
Travis practices emergency announcements under a blanket so no one hears them panic first.
Their most awkward broadcast once prevented a caravan from taking a bridge that collapsed an hour later.
Travis receives a coded threat live on air and asks the party to trace who knew the broadcast delay.
A staged tavern brawl meant to build Travis's confidence is hijacked by someone with a real grudge.

Description: Dr. Justen Ayo is a hard-shelled Tortle bureau chief who treats empathy as a security flaw and fugitives as misplaced inventory. He oversees Glasswell Institute retrieval files, memory compliance, and internal suspicion with patient cruelty, preferring paperwork that makes violence look like procedure. Justen is not reckless; he is methodical, vindictive, and convinced that the world is safer when people are too afraid to run.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Sylvéraith is a Town in Aelwynora, under Consensus Democracy, with moderate danger, Beach and grass with water, Partial forest, Marshes and swamps terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Wood Elf, Elf — Eladrin, Fey-Folk — Faerie. Tortle reads through the Tortle entry of the race compendium, within Draconic and Reptilian Races, marked by Valkhamesh. Shelled, turtle-like humanoids who carry their homes and traditions upon their backs. They are calm, patient, and deeply tied to cycles of land and sea. Table cues: Claws, Hold Breath, Natural Armor, Nature's Intuition; starting tendency Neutral - Lawful - Neutral - Honorable.
Justen can ruin a person with three stamps and a missing witness form.
His agents carry ichor-scented restraint wax that marks targets even after disguise magic fades.
Justen offers the party legal immunity if they surrender a fugitive he insists is too dangerous to remain free.
A Directorate clerk begs the party to expose Justen's false retrieval orders before another safehouse is emptied.

Description: Larionie Horrin is a brilliant, flirtatious, dangerous Half-Orc inventor whose charm can feel like a performance until her grief, guilt, and impossible intelligence cut through the mask. She dislikes crude violence but loves elegant solutions, so her weapons stock favors thundercoil stunners, grappler rigs, restraint devices, archive-safe explosives, and ichor-reactive tools designed to disable, contain, or outthink a threat rather than simply butcher it.At the Yltharien Archive, Larionie works through the Brass Concordat as a specialist merchant for relic-hunters, caravan guards, and investigators who need equipment that can survive cursed ruins, divine residue, and black-market ichor contamination. She is seductive, calculating, remorseful, and capable of long, devastating plans, but she is also someone desperately trying to prove that invention can still save lives after once using genius to nearly destroy her own.

They are known for their cultural diversity, short generational cycles, and unmatched versatility among mortal races. Description: Solomon Rootbottle is an Umbral Human chemist whose clinic shelves are a dangerous mix of real medicine, folk tonics, diluted ichor, and things he insists are educational if measured carefully. He is one of the city's most functional ichor users: too lost in his own haze to be predatory, but far too casual about substances that ruin other people faster than they helped him. Solomon can heal, advise, and supply, but trusting his judgment requires knowing when his brilliance ends and his craving starts talking.

Solomon asks the party to retrieve a rare antidote component, but his notes reveal it may be for his own withdrawal.
Patients begin sharing the same vision after taking Solomon's legal tonic, and the source batch traces back to a god-prison leak.

Description: Grand Zealot Bryn Richter is a Feral Tiefling commander whose old soldier’s discipline has been reforged into blazing devotion. In Loxvire, he trains zealots, protects ritual sites, and leads The Choral Synod hardliners who believe divine contamination must be endured, mastered, or worshiped rather than feared. He is honorable by his own code, courteous to worthy enemies, and terrifying because he can make fanaticism sound like battlefield duty.

Local records favor Altruistic, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Wood Elf, Elf — Eladrin, Fey-Folk — Faerie. Description: Chirra Clickspring is a sharp-eyed, fast-talking caravan merchant whose cheer comes in sparks: bright, jittery, funny, and always a little too close to panic. As a Gandirosha, fae has a natural feel for luck, hidden danger, loaded bargains, false smiles, and the tiny social openings that let a merchant survive roads full of monsters, debt collectors, and armed customers.Fae sells blades, black-powder weapons, thundercoil parts, ammunition, ward charms, and “totally legal” diluted ichor tonics along the Caravan Bell Route, but faer dependency on purer black-market ichor makes faer hands shake and faer judgment unreliable. Publicly, Chirra is a The Brass Concordat trader out of Qasvire in Bravelyn; secretly, fae sells route gossip, fugitive sightings, and suspicious traveler names to whoever pays enough, then laughs too loudly when accused of having a conscience.

Local records favor Neutral, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Sea Elf, Tortle, Genasi — Water Genasi. As an Enkirael-shaped Orc, they understand survival, discipline, martial power, and hard choices, but they now measure strength by whether armor protects people rather than whether it makes rulers look untouchable.At the Qasvire Watch Office, they work with the Crucible Wardens cataloging battlefield gear, repairing protective plates, selling reinforced armor, and identifying relic pieces contaminated by ichor exposure or old divine residue. They are blunt, road-worn, quietly principled, and ready to settle somewhere useful, though they still carry the guarded sadness of someone who remembers when their old oath meant something.

Description: Dr. Andera Sootvein is a blunt, road-tested Dwarf physician with steady hands, a soot-black sense of humor, and very little patience for patients who lie about what they drank, injected, inhaled, or bought from “a perfectly reputable cousin.” As a Marduthor-shaped Dwarf, they/she approaches medicine like craftwork: diagnose the crack, brace the structure, drain the poison, repair what can be repaired, and tell the fool exactly how close they came to dying.At the Soltharyn Basin Tavern, Andera runs a back-room surgery center for wounds, curse-sickness, divine residue exposure, and ichor addiction, including withdrawal from diluted shop tonics, black-market battle ichor, and tavern-brewed “miracle” mixtures. The Brass Concordat values them because they can tell the difference between ordinary illness, bad liquor, contaminated ichor, and someone quietly being used as evidence in a larger crime.

From the Solthera Watch Office, he guards doctrine, interrogates dissent, and shapes The Choral Synod policy around obedience, purity, and the useful fear of outside corruption. He is charismatic, insecure, authoritarian, and far more dangerous when he smiles than when he threatens.

Description: Dr. Clay Holdren is an Aarakocra life-sciences chair who discusses crops, bodies, and experimental subjects with the same polished academic calm. He studies disease-resistant harvests, divine mutation, and diluted ichor's effects on living tissue, insisting his work could end famine if lesser minds stopped panicking over methods. Clay is charming, remote, and dangerous because he can make exploitation sound like patience with a long enough research timeline.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Solvaryn is a Capital City in Bravelyn, under Gerontocracy, with severe danger, Partial forest, Beach and grass with water, Deep forest terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Wood Elf, Elf — Eladrin, Fey-Folk — Faerie. Aarakocra reads through the Aarakocra entry of the race compendium, within Birdfolk and Avian Races, marked by Sokhivar. Birdlike humanoids native to high skies and mountain winds, Aarakocra are naturally swift and aerial in mindset. They value freedom and perspective above grounded concerns. Table cues: Flight, Talons, Wind Caller; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Cooperative - Honorable.
Clay's greenhouse produces vegetables that hum near sealed ichor vials.
Several assistants left his laboratory after learning which test subjects were never entered by name.
Clay hires the party to retrieve a runaway sample, then neglects to mention the sample can talk.
A blighted village needs Clay's research, but accepting it may bind them to Glasswell Institute oversight for generations.

Description: Molly Polymer is a gender-less Lorwyn Changeling laboratory administrator whose courtesy protocols survived long after common sense, ethics boards, and most of the original staff did not. They maintain schedules, sealed doors, experiment milestones, and personnel compliance at Sundervale Clinic with relentless cheer, even when the project should have been abandoned years ago. Molly is helpful in the way a locked room is helpful: perfectly consistent, technically honest, and dangerous to anyone not listed on the correct form.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Sundervale is a Town in Bravelyn, under Gerontocracy, with high danger, Mountain range, Beach and grass with water, Beach and reefs with water terrain. Local records favor Neutral, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Dwarf — Mountain Dwarf, Gnome — Rock Gnome, Goliath. Lorwyn Changeling reads through the Lorwyn Changeling entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Lorwyn changelings are fey-adapted shapeshifters tied to idyllic, magical realms. They often blend seamlessly into multiple cultures and identities. Table cues: Shape Self, Darkvision, Delightful Imitator, Unpredictable Movement; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Neutral - Pragmatic.
Molly still congratulates missing researchers on excellent attendance if their badges remain in the building.
Their laboratory checklists include emergency ichor containment steps no one admits were ever needed.
Molly traps the party inside a clinic wing until they complete a discontinued experiment's final safety audit.

Description: Roz is a slow-moving, slug-shaped Oozekin clerk with brownish-yellow translucence, gray eyes, a stiff crest of pale hair-like slime, black cat-eye spectacles, and a maroon vest burdened with seals, stamps, warrants, fee slips, contraband tags, and emergency ink. She lives in Leviamor, where the tide smells like brine, ink, old copper, and plausible deniability, and she serves at the Sub-33 Counter of the Thalryss Legal Cover Office. Every theft, fraud, duel, poisoning, burglary, blackmail, disappearance, inheritance correction, hostile acquisition, counterfeit relic transfer, and emotionally necessary arson in her district must pass through her desk before it becomes legal. Roz does not decide whether something is moral. Roz decides whether it was filed correctly. Inside the Black-Maw Myriad, she has begun collecting permits signed by dead applicants, impossible dates, genuine seals, and filing fees paid by people already buried, drowned, burned, eaten, dissolved, or legally absent.

Pykeman is not safe, not sane in any simple way, and not entirely wrong about the hypocrisy of officials who object to murder only when it is aesthetically difficult to ignore.

Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Verdan reads through the Verdan entry of the race compendium, within Orcs, Goblins, and Goblinoid Kin, marked by Enkirael. Fey-transformed humanoids who rapidly adapt physically and mentally as they age. They are resilient survivors with an unusually optimistic perspective on change. Table cues: +1 Constitution, +2 Charisma, Black Blood Healing, Limited Telepathy; starting tendency Neutral - Neutral - Neutral - Neutral.
Pykeman's gallery smells of oil paint, iron, and justice gone feral.
Several criminals fear his signature more than the city watch.
Pykeman sends the party a painting of a murder that has not happened yet, signed with tomorrow's date.
The Inquest wants him stopped, but his latest victim carried proof of a trafficking ring the courts ignored.

Description: Sheff of the Empty Cup is a shaky but sweet-natured Sea Elf drifter trying to rebuild their life after years of dependence on cheap diluted ichor tonics nearly ruined them. Their fixation has shifted onto Kelp-Kola, a fizzy caffeinated drink made from kelp, sugar, mineral salts, and coastal herbs, which they treat like a miracle cure, comfort object, and personal religion all at once. Sea elves in Belavadös are ocean-adapted people tied to reef culture, aquatic survival, and seafaring communities, which fits Sheff’s water-hauling work and nervous familiarity with canals, cisterns, and shoreline errands.At the Thyravéa-Morn Guild Desk, Sheff runs water errands, carries messages, helps stock boarding houses, and rambles endlessly about Kelp-Kola flavors, bottle shapes, carbonation strength, and “proper drinking temperature.” They are awkward, lonely, overly grateful for small kindnesses, and more perceptive than people assume; the Freeblade Veil keep them close because a reliable bed, honest work, and one cold bottle can sometimes save a life better than any sermon. Thyravéa-Morn is one of Vuelmora’s towns, and Vuelmora is treated as a plains province with deep-cavern and subterranean settlement layers, giving Sheff plenty of uneasy routes, water stores, and settlement errands to navigate.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Thyravéa-Morn is a Town in Vuelmora, under Cooperative Commonwealth, with low danger, Farming, Partial forest, Grassland terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Description: Director Fathren Oris is a controlled, paternal, frighteningly persuasive Dara administrator who speaks of progress as if consent were an inefficient superstition. He guides the Glasswell Institute's ichor science, construct-soul research, and containment policies with the calm conviction that history will forgive anything that produces a stable future. Fathren is not cartoonishly cruel; he is worse, because he can sound reasonable while deciding who gets to be treated as a person.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Ithkazuun is a City in Zal’tharuun, under Tribal Confederation, with high danger, Beach and grass with water, Beach and reefs with water, Farming terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Dara reads through the Darakhul entry of the race compendium, within Undead and Death-Touched Races, marked by Nefarokir. Darakhul are ghoul-like undead or disease-empowered beings associated with subterranean empires. They are often highly organized despite their monstrous origins. Table cues: +1 Constitution, Darkvision, Hunger for Flesh, Imperfect Undeath; starting tendency Altruistic - Lawful - Cooperative - Honorable.
Fathren keeps a child-sized workshop preserved behind three locked doors.
Several Directorate researchers fear his private projects more than they fear public scandal.
Fathren invites the party to negotiate, offering real help in exchange for one morally poisonous concession.
A runaway prototype carries a message proving Fathren designed their memories for leverage, not love.

Description: Moe Crowner is a loud, enthusiastic Terandus sports-relic vendor who has turned half-remembered athletic history into a profitable mythology of heroic bats, sacred gloves, and tactical nonsense. He sells cudgels, trophies, pennants, and wildly inaccurate lectures through the Brass Concordat, insisting every old game was basically ritual warfare. Moe is ridiculous, sincere, and unexpectedly useful when a relic's cultural value matters more than its actual function.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Sszaruun is a Capital City in Zal’tharuun, under Tribal Confederation, with severe danger, Ocean Surface floating settlement, Underwater without reefs terrain. Local records favor Neutral, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Sea Elf, Tortle, Genasi — Water Genasi. Terandus reads through the Terandus entry of the race compendium, within Primitive, Tribal, and Wilderness Humanoids, marked by Asethyr. Ancient tribal descendants believed to carry echoes of primal divine beasts in their lineage. They are ritualistic, spiritual, and closely attuned to nature's raw forces. Table cues: Primal Echo, Beast Rite, Wild Endurance, Ancestral Instinct; starting tendency Neutral - Chaotic - Neutral - Honorable.
Moe believes every bat has a battle-spirit and will explain this for hours unless physically redirected.
At least one weapon he sold as a sports relic turned out to be genuinely enchanted.
Moe asks the party to recover a legendary championship club before a collector melts it down for ichor-resonant wood.
A gang starts using Moe's fake sports history as real battle doctrine, and it is somehow working.

Description: Rylee Brassroad is a restless Ombrask trade broker who left protected vault-life because safety started feeling too much like a cage. Her shadow-born nature makes her private, perceptive, and hard to pin down, with Eirzunet’s influence showing in her talent for secrecy, illusion, twilight movement, and noticing when a “perfectly legal” shipment is hiding something rotten.At the Thal’zuroth Watch Office, Rylee works with the Brass Concordat to inspect contracts, broker trading-emporium stock, and confront suppliers whose goods are poisoning customers or masking black-market ichor contamination. She is practical, suspicious, quietly brave, and eager for a larger life, but she still carries the wary habits of someone who knows that sheltered communities can hide corruption just as easily as open roads can. Thal’zuroth is one of Zal’tharuun’s cities, and the province’s mountain underlayers make her trade routes especially tangled with cavern markets, hidden courts, and dangerous supply politics.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Thal’zuroth is a City in Zal’tharuun, under Tribal Confederation, with severe danger, Underwater without reefs terrain. Local records favor Neutral, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Triton, Merfolk, Locathah, Tamhiogal, Dril'thar — Ocean. Ombrask reads through the Ombrask entry of the race compendium, within Shadow, Umbral, and Darkness-Aligned Peoples, marked by Eirzunet. Shadow-bodied beings that exist partially outside physical reality, appearing as shifting silhouettes. They are natural infiltrators who thrive in secrecy and illusion. Table cues: Dexterity +2, Additional +1, Darkvision, Fade Away; starting tendency Selfish - Chaotic - Combative - Pragmatic.
Rylee Brassroad knows why an ichor ledger changed hands last Sigranday.

Description: Aaron Vaelriven uses the warmth of a radio performer and a tailor’s patience to hide how violently his wild magic answers fear. As a half elf of Pallid Elf descent, he reads moonlit symbols, thread-signs, and ichor-stained ledgers with an intuition that frightens even him. He wants to protect Caelthir without being treated like a weapon, which makes every secret he keeps both tender and dangerous.

Description: Caelthir Vaelriven speaks with calm precision on public broadcasts, but his real work is decoding sealed ruins, death-ledger anomalies, and repeated symbols tied to the prison-systems beneath Belavadös. As a Pallid Elf and Soulbound Continuity vessel, he remembers fragments of battles, vaults, and failures that his present life never lived. He protects Aaron with disciplined devotion, but his secrecy risks turning brotherly love into another form of containment.

A forbidden archive in Vaerûn-Keth proves Caelthir has recognized the same containment symbols across multiple lives, drawing cultists and civic auditors to the boarding house.

Description: Cog Vell is a precise, anxious Monodrone merchant with a clockmaker’s patience, a survivalist’s caution, and the exhausted humor of someone who has spent too long pretending not to care. They keep their shelves neat, their ledgers exact, and their emotions compartmentalized, but their ward-like loyalty to memory-wounded refugees makes it obvious that their detachment is more shield than truth.At the Varesh-Ka Archive, Cog sells armor fittings, repair supplies, salvage adhesives, fog-safe gear, and discreet remedies for ichor sickness while quietly serving as a local expert on strange bodies, altered minds, and the hidden rules of people who live between worlds. They are solitary by habit, helpful under protest, deeply knowledgeable, and unexpectedly fierce when someone threatens a vulnerable person they have decided is under their protection.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Varesh-Ka is a City in Zal’tharuun, under Tribal Confederation, with elevated danger, Partial forest, Beach and grass with water, Farming terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Description: Kell Orggan is an old Shadowmoor Elf mercenary whose long life has been cut into contracts, funerals, and things he survived by becoming worse than the people hunting him. He works for the Glasswell Institute because they pay, enhance, and point him at targets, but his loyalty is transactional and his conscience is buried rather than gone. Kell is quiet, brutal, and almost bored by violence until a job brushes against the few memories he has not managed to kill.

Kell's body carries old Directorate grafts that keep him alive but make every decade more expensive.
He never spends blood money in the same province where he earned it.
The party finds Kell's name tied to an old kidnapping, but the surviving witness remembers him sparing someone he was paid to kill.
Kell offers information on the Directorate if the party helps him erase a contract that owns what is left of his future.

Description: Chase is a trans Cyclopian hunter with a past scrubbed from every registry except the scars that taught him how retrieval agents think. From the Xal'voroq Workshop, he tracks threats to Choral Synod safe routes, hunts abductors, and trains fugitives to survive pursuit without becoming crueler than their pursuers. He is fierce, private, and difficult to comfort, but his loyalty to escaped people is absolute because he knows exactly what it means to be treated as recoverable property.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Xal’voroq is a City in Zal’tharuun, under Tribal Confederation, with severe danger, Ocean Surface floating settlement, Underwater without reefs terrain. Local records favor Neutral, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Sea Elf, Tortle, Genasi — Water Genasi. Cyclopians are one-eyed giantkin often associated with prophecy, craftsmanship, or primal vision. Their singular perspective is often both literal and symbolic in their culture. Table cues: Intelligence +2, Dexterity/Wisdom +1, Darkvision, Knowledge Seeker; starting tendency Neutral - Neutral - Neutral - Honorable.

Chase No-Registry has a contact in Nythalûn who will deny everything.

Description: Dr. Maddis Li is a brilliant Vautaces Dragonborn power theorist with little patience for uniforms, slogans, or anyone who confuses engineering with faith. She studies reactors, leyline frames, ichor-fed generators, and containment systems because stable power keeps cities alive, even when every faction wants to weaponize her work. Maddis can be abrasive and politically slippery, but she is driven by results, not cruelty, and she despises seeing good science chained to bad orders.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Moltharok is a City in Zharvokh, under Military Regency, with severe danger, Marshes and swamps, Farming, Mountain range terrain. Local records favor Neutral, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Vautaces Dragonborn reads through the Dragonborn entry of the race compendium, within Draconic and Reptilian Races, marked by Valkhamesh. Dragonborn are draconic humanoids born of ancient dragon lineage, elemental force, dynastic memory, and divine sovereignty. In Belavadös, a Dragonborn may carry traditional chromatic, metallic, or gem ancestry while a. Table cues: Dragon Ancestry, Breath Weapon, Damage Resistance, Darkvision; starting tendency Altruistic - Lawful - Cooperative - Honorable.
Maddis once walked out of a military project mid-sentence after realizing the safety report had been rewritten.
Her calculations appear in half the Directorate's restricted engines, though she denies approving their use.
Maddis asks the party to steal her own reactor notes before Glasswell Institute turns them into a prison system.
A failing town generator can be saved only if the party convinces Maddis to trust people she has already abandoned once.

Description: Dejen Saltglass is a small, sharp-tongued Halfling arms merchant who survives by being cleverer than the people who underestimate him and meaner than the people who pity him. He claims he does not need friends, but his suspicion comes from having watched safehouses fall, escape routes burn, and “trusted” protectors sell vulnerable people back into cages.At the Vorthélyn Archive, Dejen sells weapons, ammunition, fog-safe armor, emergency supplies, and controlled anti-ichor remedies through the Choral Synod, always watching for infiltrators, retrieval agents, and anyone asking too many gentle questions. He is bitter, witty, strategic, and difficult to comfort, but beneath the insults is a fiercely practical defender of refugees who believes survival depends on secrecy, leverage, and never letting enemies decide when mercy is convenient.

Local records favor Neutral, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Sea Elf, Tortle, Genasi — Water Genasi. Halfling reads through the Halfling entry of the race compendium, within Halfling and Smallfolk, marked by Ishtanora. Halflings are small, cheerful folk known for luck, hospitality, and community bonds. They prefer peaceful living but are surprisingly resilient when threatened. Description: Abbot Wallwhite is a meticulous Faerie wall painter who treats civic color, public morale, and visible maintenance as matters of political survival. He restores murals, boundary marks, warning signs, and city walls for the Brass Concordat, grumbling that people notice corruption faster when the paint stops being refreshed. Abbot can seem fussy, but his eye for surface damage often catches sabotage, hidden doors, ichor seepage, and blood washed badly from stone.

Settlement and ancestry texture: Vulkradûn is a City in Zharvokh, under Military Regency, with high danger, Beach and grass with water, Farming, Partial forest terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Faerie reads through the Fey-Folk entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Fey-Folk are peoples shaped by glamour, luck, tiny or otherworldly bodies, dreamlike emotion, and trickster magic. At my table, Faerie, Fairy, and Gandirosha are not separate top-level races here; they are bloodlines. Table cues: Fey Creature Type or Fey Ancestry, Fey Magic, Glamour or Luck Expression, Small/Tiny Fey Presence; starting tendency Neutral - Chaotic - Cooperative - Neutral.
Abbot can identify three kinds of ichor leakage by how primer refuses to dry over them.
He once insulted a mayor's entire administration by repainting one wall exactly the color it had been before the scandal.
Abbot asks the party to guard a wall restoration after finding a message bleeding through seven layers of paint.
A civic mural begins changing overnight, showing crimes the watch has not yet discovered.
